**Description**
CADCraft crashes every time it is launched normally on my system, before I can use the application. Updating the Intel graphics driver did not resolve the issue.

**Environment**
- CADCraft 0.3.0
- Windows 10 Pro 64-bit, version 22H2, build 19045
- Lenovo ThinkPad L580
- Intel Core i7-8550U
- Intel UHD Graphics 620

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Launch CADCraft normally, without a graphics-backend environment override.
2. The application crashes during startup and creates a crash dump.

**Expected behavior**
CADCraft starts normally.

title: i18n: add Ukrainian (uk) interface translation
author: dmatviichuk
body:
CADCraft currently displays its interface in English and has no language selector. I would like to add Ukrainian (`uk`, shown as **Українська**) and contribute the implementation from my fork.

The sibling Craft apps already have a useful pattern for this:

- [VectorCraft #205](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/205): UTF-8 TSV catalogs, English fallback, translation at display time, and live language switching.
- [PdfCraft #106](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/106): the same catalog convention and a persisted interface-language preference.
- [FilmCraft #238](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/238): catalog coverage checks and system-language selection.

Proposed scope:

- Add a small localization layer in `cadcraft-ui-egui` and an original Ukrainian catalog under the project license.
- Translate menus (including the native macOS menus), tooltips, panels, dialogs, and the application shell.
- Provide Auto / English / Українська selection, remember the choice, and recognize Ukrainian locale tags such as `uk-UA` and `uk_UA.UTF-8`.
- Keep command IDs, command-line keywords, file formats, drawing names, CLI/MCP responses, and automation identifiers stable; translate only text shown to the user.
- Test catalog validity and coverage, locale resolution, persistence, live switching, and Ukrainian glyph coverage; run the existing quality gates and inspect the rendered UI.

Translations will be written from the meaning of CADCraft's English strings, without copying proprietary localization resources. This also provides the foundation for future languages.

title: Scripts: keyword prompts like POLYGON's [Inscribed/Circumscribed] swallow the rest of the line, so `POLYGON 6 200,20 I 15` silently draws nothing
author: wzsxb233
body:
**Summary**

In a script, POLYGON fails without any error if the Inscribed/Circumscribed keyword and the radius are on the same line. `POLYGON 6 200,20 I 15` draws nothing, but the same input with a newline after `I` draws the hexagon. In AutoCAD `.scr` files a space acts as Enter at this prompt.

The cause seems to be that this prompt is declared `Accept::TEXT` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/draw.rs:699`). `Session::script` hands the whole rest of the line to any prompt where `accept.text && !accept.point`, so the prompt receives the input `I 15`. That doesn't match a keyword, and the command quietly ends. Other keyword-only prompts declared the same way probably behave the same, for example MIRROR "Erase source objects? [Yes/No]" (`modify.rs:1384`), the constraint-type prompts in `constraints.rs` and DIMOVERRIDE.

**Environment**
- CADCraft `main` @ 86f3199 (v0.3.0), `cadcraft-cli` release build
- Linux x86_64 (Debian 13), Rust 1.99

**Steps to reproduce**
```sh
cadcraft-cli run --script 'POLYGON 6 200,20 I 15\n' --save a.dxf && cadcraft-cli info a.dxf   # counts: {}
cadcraft-cli run --script 'POLYGON 6 200,20 I\n15\n' --save b.dxf && cadcraft-cli info b.dxf  # counts: {Polyline: 1}
```
Other variants:
- `POLYGON 6 200,20 C 15\n` draws nothing.
- `POLYGON 6 200,20\nI 15\n` draws nothing.
- `POLYGON\n6\n200,20\nI\n15\n` works.
- `CIRCLE 0,0 D 20\n` works. That is a keyword at a point/number prompt.

**Expected**
At keyword-only prompts, a space should end the input like Enter does, as at other prompts and as in AutoCAD scripts. `POLYGON 6 200,20 I 15` should draw an inscribed hexagon with radius 15. If the input doesn't match any keyword, the command line should at least print an error rather than end silently.

**Actual**
No entity is created, no error is printed, and the script carries on, so later geometry depends on a polygon that doesn't exist.

**Possible fix**
Give pure keyword prompts their own accept mode, or make `script()` (and the command line) split on spaces…

title: Add Light and System interface themes that follow the macOS light/dark appearance
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Add Light and System interface themes to CADCraft, with System following the macOS light/dark appearance live, so the app changes with the rest of the desktop when macOS switches appearance automatically.

## Problem to solve

macOS can switch between Light and Dark appearance automatically (System Settings → Appearance → Auto changes it at sunset and sunrise), and many Mac apps offer a "System" theme choice that tracks it.

CADCraft has a single, hardcoded dark interface. `Tokens::get()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` always returns `Tokens::DARK`, the app installs `Visuals::dark()` once at startup, and `UiState` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` has no theme field. No menu or dialog offers a theme choice.

CADCraft has no light theme and no way to follow the OS, so it stays dark while macOS and other apps are in Light mode.

Add a light interface theme, and a theme choice with three options: System, Light and Dark. Light and Dark fix the theme. System applies Light or Dark to match the current macOS appearance at launch and switches immediately when the OS appearance changes while the app is open. The saved choice stays System; only the displayed theme changes.

1. The app has a light interface theme that covers every surface it paints itself (drawing canvas chrome, ribbon, palettes, command line and status bar), not only standard widgets, with readable contrast throughout.

title: SETVAR DIMSCALE is accepted but never applied to dimensions (style scale always wins)
author: slackerchris
body:
**Version:** 0.3.0 (Linux x86_64 .deb), reproduced via `cadcraft-cli mcp`

**Steps**
1. New drawing; `execute setvar {"name": "DIMSCALE", "value": 24}` → returns `{"name": "DIMSCALE", "value": 24.0}`
2. `line 0,0 100,0`, then `dimlinear 0,0 100,0 50,-20`
3. Render: the dimension text and arrows are drawn at scale 1 (text ~0.18 units tall)

**Expected:** As in AutoCAD, setting DIMSCALE applies to dimensions created afterwards.

**Cause (looks like):** [`crates/render/src/dim.rs:366`](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/86f3199b400c271a1166103519b3785e4ac88e72/crates/render/src/dim.rs#L366) only falls back to the header DIMSCALE when the style's `scale` is ≤ 0:

```rust
let k = if st.scale > 0.0 && st.scale.is_finite() { st.scale } else { dimscale.max(1e-9) };
```

Standard ships with `scale = 1.0`, so the sysvar never takes effect on dimensions. Other places treat it differently, so they disagree with the dimension geometry:
- [`crates/doc/src/extents.rs:83`](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/86f3199b400c271a1166103519b3785e4ac88e72/crates/doc/src/extents.rs#L83) multiplies style scale × header DIMSCALE when computing extents
- [`crates/render/src/lib.rs:506`](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/86f3199b400c271a1166103519b3785e4ac88e72/crates/render/src/lib.rs#L506) sizes leader arrowheads with the header DIMSCALE only (ignoring the style scale)

**Workaround:** `dimstyle {"name": "Standard", "DIMSCALE": 24}` scales new dimensions correctly.

Possibly related: #30 (SETVAR at the command line).

title: LINE command cannot snap first point to tangent because prompt has no base point
author: nusuns
body:
Title: LINE command cannot snap first point to tangent because prompt has no base point

Description:
When drawing a `LINE`, the tangent object snap (TAN) works for the *second* point but not for the *first* point. This makes it impossible to start a line tangent to a circle, e.g., drawing a belt/chain line that is tangent to a large circle and then tangent to a smaller circle.

## Reproduction steps
1. Draw two circles of different sizes.
2. Start the `LINE` command.
3. Hover over the first (large) circle with Tangent snap enabled (running or via override).
   - No tangent snap marker appears.
4. Click a freehand point near the first circle to set the line start.
5. Hover over the second (small) circle.
   - Tangent snap marker appears normally.

## Expected behavior
Tangent snap should work for the first point of a line, just like it does for subsequent points.

## Actual behavior
The first point cannot snap tangent to a circle. The second point can.

## Why it happens (source analysis)
In `crates/engine/src/cmd/draw.rs`, the `LineM` prompt only sets a `base` point after the first point is picked:

```rust
fn prompt(&self, _s: &Session) -> Prompt {
    match self.pts.len() {
        0 => Prompt::new("Specify first point", Accept::POINT),
        1 | 2 => Prompt::new("Specify next point", Accept::POINT)
                     .kw(&["Undo"])
                     .base_opt(self.pts.last().copied()),
        ...
    }
}
```

The canvas calls `snap::osnap(..., base)`, where `base` is taken from `prompt.base`. Tangent/perpendicular snaps in `crates/engine/src/snap.rs` only compute tangent points when `base` is `Some(...)`:

```rust
if let Some(bp) = base {
    ...
    if osmode & mode::TAN != 0 {
        ...
        cands.extend(c.tangent_points(bp).into_iter().map(|t| (mode::TAN, t)));
    }
}
```

Because the first-point prompt has `base = None`, the tangent candidate is never generated.

## Suggested fix
Allow the first point of a line (and other "start point" prompts)…

title: fix(layer): delete and purge remove a layer still used by an inserted block
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

A line inside an inserted block can still reference a layer after `layer.delete` or `purge` removes that layer. In the reproduced drawing, the layer list reports `A` as used, but both commands remove it while keeping the block and its geometry. The line's SVG export changes from red to black, and saving and reopening DXF preserves the missing layer and changed color.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the baseline CLI described under Runtime or environment. Run these commands in an empty writable working directory. The first command creates the fixture through supported drawing commands; no external drawing is required.

1. Create a red layer `A`, move one line onto it, and convert that line into an inserted block. The current layer stays `0`, so the insert is on `0` while the line inside the block is on `A`.

```sh
cadcraft-cli run \
  --cmd 'layer.new {"name":"A","color":"red"}' \
  --cmd 'line {"points":[[0,0],[10,10]]}' \
  --cmd 'selectall {}' \
  --cmd 'properties.set {"layer":"A"}' \
  --cmd 'block {"name":"BLK","base":[0,0],"keep":"convert"}' \
  --cmd 'layer {}' --cmd 'blocks.list {}' \
  --cmd 'drawing.inspect {"entities":true}' \
  --save before.dxf --export before.svg
```

2. Test deletion and purge independently from that fixture, then inspect and save each result.

  --cmd 'vplayer {"handle":"100","freeze":["Walls"]}' \
  --cmd 'properties {"handles":["100"]}' \
  --cmd 'layout.set {"name":"Control"}' \
  --cmd 'viewport.set {"handle":"101","center":[56,78],"viewHeight":125,"locked":true}' \
  --cmd 'properties {"handles":["101"]}' \
  --save viewport-freeze.dxf

```sh

  --cmd 'layout.set {"name":"Frozen"}' \
  --cmd 'properties {"handles":["100"]}' \
  --cmd 'layout.set {"name":"Control"}' \

title: SHX fonts render as empty boxes for CJK text; request TTF fallback mapping (and .ttc support)
author: aaronclaw26-crypto
body:
CADCraft v0.4.0 (commit `43e33ad`) reads CJK text from DWG correctly, but text styles that use SHX fonts render every CJK glyph as an empty box.

Real-world drawings from Taiwan use `chineset.shx` (big font), `@ae.shx`, `aehalf.shx`, and `romans.shx`. A minimal one-line title gives 14 empty boxes. With the style switched to a CJK TTF (`LINESeedTW_TTF_Rg.ttf`), it gives 0 boxes.

Cause, in v0.4.0:
- [`ttf.rs#L92`](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/v0.4.0/crates/fonts/src/ttf.rs#L92): `find()` returns `None` for `.shx` names.
- [`lib.rs#L158`](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/v0.4.0/crates/fonts/src/lib.rs#L158): an unresolved font falls back to `TextFont::Stroke`.
- [`lib.rs#L105`](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/v0.4.0/crates/fonts/src/lib.rs#L105): a missing glyph draws an empty box.
- [`ttf.rs#L51`](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/v0.4.0/crates/fonts/src/ttf.rs#L51): the font scan skips `.ttc`, which excludes most macOS CJK system fonts.

Requests, smallest first:
1. A fallback map from SHX to TTF (like AutoCAD's FONTALT / fontmap), for example a default CJK TTF used when an SHX big font can't be resolved.
2. Include `.ttc` in the font scan.
3. Native SHX and big-font rendering later (ROADMAP M4).

Thanks!

title: Entity transparency can't be set and isn't saved: `properties.set` ignores `transparency`, DXF drops group 440
author: kaffeochknivar
body:
Found while fixing layer transparency in DXF (#96, PR #131). Per-object transparency is missing end to end:

1. **It can't be set.** `properties.set` documents `transparency?` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/props.rs:14`), but `run_set` never reads the key:

   ```sh
   cadcraft-cli run --cmd 'line {"points":[[0,0],[10,0]]}' \
     --cmd 'properties.set {"handles":["100"],"transparency":50}' \
     --cmd 'drawing.inspect {"entities":true}'
   ```

   This returns `{"changed":1}`, but the entity keeps `Transparency::ByLayer`. The only command that changes the field today is MATCHPROP, which copies it (`props.rs:306`).

2. **It isn't shown.** The Properties palette's Transparency row is a fixed "ByLayer" box (`crates/ui-egui/src/palettes.rs:655`). Neither `properties` nor `drawing.inspect` reports the value.

3. **It isn't saved or read.** No entity writes group 440, and the reader ignores it. So entity transparency in an AutoCAD DXF is lost when the file is opened, and lost again on save.

**Expected:**
- `properties.set` accepts `"ByLayer"`, `"ByBlock"` or a percentage 0–90.
- The Properties palette edits it, and `properties` reports it.
- Entities round-trip group 440, using the DXF Reference encoding: 0 = ByLayer, `0x01000000` = ByBlock, `0x02000000 | alpha` = a fixed transparency. That is the same encoding PR #131 uses for layers (`transparency_to_dxf` / `transparency_from_dxf` in `dxf_ext.rs`).

title: [Bug] macOS: opening a .dxf from Finder fails ("CADCraft cannot open files in the Drawing Exchange Format format")
author: ripleyXLR8
body:
## Summary
On macOS, CADCraft.app registers itself for `.dxf` / `.dwg` (`CFBundleDocumentTypes` in `Info.plist`), but opening a drawing through LaunchServices — double-click in Finder, *Open With → CADCraft*, or `open -a CADCraft file.dxf` — fails with the system alert:

> The document "drawing.dxf" could not be opened. CADCraft cannot open files in the "Drawing Exchange Format" format.

## Cause (from reading the source)
`apps/cadcraft/src/main.rs` only collects files from `std::env::args()`, and `crates/ui-egui` handles `dropped_files`. Nothing handles the macOS "open documents" Apple Event (`application:openURLs:` / `kAEOpenDocuments`), which is how LaunchServices passes files to a bundled app (it does not put them in argv). Because the bundle advertises document types but never accepts the event, AppKit shows the generic "cannot open files in the … format" error. This also means a file can't be sent from Finder to an already-running instance.

Workaround: pass the path as an argument (`open -n -a CADCraft --args /path/drawing.dxf`) or drag the file onto the window.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Install `cadcraft-0.4.0-macos-universal.dmg`.
2. In Finder, right-click any `.dxf` (e.g. `examples/apartment.dxf`) → Open With → CADCraft (or run `open -a CADCraft apartment.dxf`).
3. CADCraft launches with an empty drawing and macOS shows the error above.

## Expected
The drawing opens (in the running instance, or a new tab/window), as with a command-line argument or drag-and-drop.

## Possible fix
Handle the open-documents event on macOS, e.g. add an `NSApplicationDelegate` `application:openURLs:` method (or an Apple Event handler for `kAEOpenDocuments`) around `eframe::run_native`, and forward the paths to the app the same way `dropped_files` are handled.

## Environment
- CADCraft 0.4.0 (build 43e33add44ffcf386f7ca0f06cfe1af7acae7256), macos-universal DMG
- macOS 15.8.1

title: [Bug] DXF --save downgrades $ACADVER to AC1015 (R2000) but keeps UTF-8 text bytes — all non-ASCII text is corrupted for any compliant reader
author: limu2021
body:
## Summary

`cadcraft-cli run <input> --save out.dxf` writes **UTF-8 encoded text bytes** while declaring `$ACADVER = AC1015` (AutoCAD R2000) and leaving `$DWGCODEPAGE = ANSI_1252`.

DXF R2000 has no UTF-8 text encoding — before R2007 the text encoding is defined by `$DWGCODEPAGE`. A compliant reader therefore decodes the UTF-8 bytes as CP1252 and every non-ASCII character is destroyed. ASCII text survives, which is what makes this easy to miss.

## Environment

- `cadcraft-cli 0.4.0`
- Windows 11 x64 (Chinese locale)
- Portable build `cadcraft-0.4.0-windows-x64-portable.zip`, sha256 `f16d437834520eaaa304102f3df22b2c9429c863e052309cdd009f98f7aee898`
- Independent reader used for verification: **ezdxf 1.4.4**

## Minimal reproduction

Generate a small R2018 DXF containing one CJK string and one ASCII string:

```python
import ezdxf
doc = ezdxf.new("R2018")
doc.styles.add("HZ", font="Deng.ttf")
msp = doc.modelspace()
msp.add_text("图号", dxfattribs={"style": "HZ", "height": 5.0, "insert": (10, 10)})
msp.add_text("PART-001", dxfattribs={"style": "HZ", "height": 5.0, "insert": (10, 25)})
doc.saveas("min_cjk.dxf")
```

Then:

```
cadcraft-cli run min_cjk.dxf --save min_cjk_cc.dxf
```

## Expected

`min_cjk_cc.dxf` reopens with `图号` and `PART-001`.

## Actual

Header comparison:

```
input   min_cjk.dxf     18,814 B   $ACADVER=AC1032   $DWGCODEPAGE=ANSI_1252
output  min_cjk_cc.dxf   8,099 B   $ACADVER=AC1015   $DWGCODEPAGE=ANSI_1252
```

The output still contains the **raw UTF-8 bytes** for `图号` (`E5 9B BE E5 8F B7`), but under R2000 those bytes mean `å›¾å·` in CP1252.

Read the output back with an independent reader:

```
original        :  '图号'
                   'PART-001'

CADCraft output :  'å›¾å\udc8f·'    <-- corrupted
                   'PART-001'        <-- fine (ASCII)
```

On a larger drawing (23 text entities, 16 of which contain CJK, 1 of which contains `Ø`):

| | original | after `--save` |
|---|---|---|
| texts containing CJK | 16 / 23 | **0 / 23** |
| texts …

title: [Bug] `extents` unions geometry ~180 m apart, so auto-fit `convert` / `--export` renders real drawings into ~5% of the canvas
author: limu2021
body:

For real-world drawings whose model space contains both a drawing body and a title-block / frame set at a large offset, `extents` unions them into one box. The auto-fit export then squeezes the actual drawing into a small corner of the image.

Measured on a 2,536-entity drawing, the rendered content occupies **4.9% of the image area** by default. Tightening the box brings that to **76.2%** — a 15× difference. There is no way to override the region from the CLI (see #165), so the only workaround is destroying entities.

Binning every geometric point of sample A by Y in 10 m bands shows two narrow content bands separated by a **180 m void**:

title: fix(engine): programmatic undo during an active command undoes the previous command
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

If you run `undo` programmatically (`engine.execute`, MCP `execute`, the control channel, or `undo {json}` in a script) while an interactive command is still running, it undoes the *previous* completed command. The running command's work is lost too. Interactive commands push their undo snapshot only when they end (`Session::finish` in `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`). So `undo` pops the earlier snapshot, which removes the earlier geometry and drops the running command's uncommitted entities, and the command keeps running from a stale `before` state.

I found this while fixing #51 (see the Limits section of #171).

## Steps to reproduce

```rust
let mut s = Session::new();
s.execute("line", &json!({"points": [[0, 0], [10, 0]]})).unwrap();
s.script("TEXT 0,0 5 0 HELLO\n").unwrap(); // TEXT stays active ("Enter text:")
s.execute("undo", &json!({})).unwrap();
```

Through MCP: `execute` a `line`, then `script` with `{"text":"TEXT 0,0 5 0 HELLO\n"}`, then `execute` with `{"command":"undo"}`.

## Expected

The same thing that happens when `undo` comes from the menu, toolbar, Cmd+Z or the command line: `Session::start` first ends the running command the way Esc does (keeping what it already drew as one undo step), and then undoes that step. The drawing keeps `[Line]`, and no command is left running.

## Actual

`undo` reports `Line`. The drawing is empty (both the line and `HELLO` are gone), and TEXT is still running with a stale `before` snapshot. Ending TEXT afterwards pushes a wrong undo step.

`redo` during an active command has the same problem: it swaps the drawing under the running command.

title: fix(dxf): saving and reopening loses saved layer states
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Saved layer states don't survive a DXF (or DWG) save. `layerstate.save` (Format ▸ Layer States Manager…) stores them in the drawing, and `layerstate.list` shows them, but the DXF writer never writes `Drawing::layer_states` and the reader never reads any. ## Steps to reproduce

```sh

  --cmd 'layer.new {"name":"Walls","color":"red"}' \
  --cmd 'layerstate.save {"name":"Plot"}' \
  --cmd 'layerstate.list {}' \
  --save ls.dxf
cadcraft-cli run ls.dxf --cmd 'layerstate.list {}'
cadcraft-cli run ls.dxf --cmd 'layerstate.restore {"name":"Plot"}'
```

The reopened drawing lists `Plot` (3 layers), and `layerstate.restore` brings back each layer's saved on/off, frozen, locked, colour, linetype, lineweight and plot settings.

{"message":"Plot","states":[{"layers":3,"name":"Plot"}]}
wrote ls.dxf (9326 bytes)

invalid parameters for `layerstate.restore`: no such layer state

title: fix(dxf): saving drops raster images and silently deletes entity types CADCraft doesn't model
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Opening a DXF/DWG made by another program and saving it deletes some objects without telling the user:

- [ ] **Raster images are dropped on save.** IMAGE entities are read (insertion point, pixel vectors, size), but the DXF writer has no case for them, so they are missing from the saved file. The reader also ignores the IMAGEDEF object, so the image's file path is empty even before saving (`path: ""`). The clip boundary, display flags and brightness/contrast/fade aren't kept either. DWG save goes through the same DXF writer, so DWG loses them too.
- [ ] **Entities CADCraft doesn't model are deleted on save without a warning.** MLINE, MULTILEADER, 3DSOLID, REGION, BODY, MESH, SURFACE, OLE2FRAME, TOLERANCE, ACAD_PROXY_ENTITY and other types are read as "Proxy" entities, with their raw group codes kept. The writer drops them all. `qsave`/`saveas` report success and the user isn't told that anything is missing.

Writing these entities back verbatim isn't safe at the moment. CADCraft writes R2000 (AC1015) DXF, and many of these types only exist in later versions (MULTILEADER, MESH, SURFACE). Others need objects the reader throws away (MLINESTYLE, MLEADERSTYLE, history objects, CLASSES entries). The ACIS data of 3DSOLID/REGION/BODY in R2013+ files is in a separate section the reader doesn't keep. A file with half-resolved references like that can be rejected as a whole by other CAD programs. So for now the save should warn about these types, and images should round-trip properly.

## Steps to reproduce

`foreign.dxf` is a small hand-written DXF. It has a LINE, an IMAGE on layer `Pics` (640×480 px, polygonal clip, brightness 60, contrast 40, fade 10) that points through group 340 to an IMAGEDEF (`images/logo.png`, named `logo` in `ACAD_IMAGE_DICT`) with its IMAGEDEF_REACTOR, an MLINE and a 3DSOLID.

```sh
cadcraft-cli info foreign.dxf                      # counts: Line 1, Raster Image 1, Proxy 2
cadcraft-cli run foreign.dxf --cmd 'entities {}'   # image "path…

title: fix(dxf): saving loses linetype text, multileader styles, page setup scale/plot style, named views, UCSs and groups
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

A round-trip check (save a drawing to DXF, reopen it, compare the drawing models) shows that several table and object-section items are lost. They are all written incompletely or not at all by `crates/io/src/dxf_write.rs`, or ignored by `dxf_read.rs`:

- [ ] **Complex linetype text and shape elements.** The LTYPE writer puts `74 0` for every dash, and the reader only looks at group 49 and ignores 74, 75, 340, 46, 50, 44, 45 and 9. This affects the built-in `FENCELINE1` linetype (`crates/doc/src/library.rs`): the embedded `o` and its scale are gone after reopening.

  cadcraft-cli run a.dxf --cmd 'mleaderstyle {}'   # current "Standard", only the Standard style

title: fix(dxf): saving loses entity thickness, point angle, hatch origin/background/elevation, xref paths and the built-in font name; polyface meshes open as polylines
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Saving a drawing to DXF and reopening it loses several properties of individual entities, blocks and text styles. A round-trip comparison of synthetic drawings (`write_dxf` → `read_dxf`, field by field) found these:

- [ ] **Entity thickness (group 39) is never written.** RECTANG's Thickness option sets it, and so can files from other programs (LINE, POINT, CIRCLE, ARC, TEXT, SOLID, TRACE, LWPOLYLINE, POLYLINE all have group 39 in the DXF Reference). The reader already reads 39; the writer never emits it, so every thickness comes back as 0.
  ```sh
  cadcraft-cli run --metric --cmd 'rectang {"p1":[0,0],"p2":[10,5],"thickness":3}' --save t.dxf
  cadcraft-cli run t.dxf --cmd 'entities {}'     # thickness 0
  ```
- [ ] **POINT angle (group 50) is never written.** A point with `angle` 0.5 rad reopens with 0. The reader already reads 50.
- [ ] **Hatch origin, background colour and elevation are lost.** The writer ignores `origin` (the pattern lines' base points 43/44 never include it, so other programs don't see the shift either) and `background`. The elevation is written as the z of the first group 10, but the reader hard-codes `elevation: 0.0`. A hatch with origin (1,2), background colour 2 and elevation 1 reopens with (0,0), no background and elevation 0.
- [ ] **Block xref flag and path are not written.** A block with `xref_path = Some("plans/site.dxf")` is written as an ordinary block: BLOCK group 70 has no xref bit (4) and group 1 is empty. The reader sets an empty path for xref-flagged blocks but never reads group 1.
- [ ] **The built-in font name doesn't survive.** The `Standard` style's font `CADCraft Stroke` is written as `txt` in STYLE group 3 (a file every reader has), which is right for other programs, but it reopens as `txt`.
  ```sh
  cadcraft-cli run --metric --save s.dxf && cadcraft-cli run s.dxf --cmd 'style.list {}'   # font "txt"
  ```
- [ ] **Polyface and polygon mesh POLYLINEs from other programs turn into bogus 3D polylines.** POLYLINE …

title: fix(draw): ELLIPSE Rotation/Parameter and BREAK First point keywords are ignored
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Three command-line keywords are offered in the prompt but have no effect, so the value typed after them is read the wrong way:

- ELLIPSE `Rotation` at "Specify distance to other axis or [Rotation]": the next value should be a rotation around the major axis (ratio = cos(angle)); it is taken as the other-axis distance instead.
- ELLIPSE (Arc) `Parameter` at "Specify start angle or [Parameter]": the next values should be ellipse parameters; they are still converted as true angles.
- BREAK `First point` at "Specify second break point or [First point]": it should ask for a new first break point (the selection pick then only selects the object); it is ignored, the pick point stays the first break point, and the remaining input is left over.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `ELLIPSE 0,0 10,0 R 60`
2. `ELLIPSE A 0,0 20,0 5 P 45 180`
3. `LINE 0,0 10,0` + Enter, then `BREAK 5,0 F 2,0 6,0`

## Expected

1. An ellipse centred at 5,0 with major half-axis 5 along X and ratio cos 60° = 0.5.
2. An elliptical arc whose start parameter is 45° (not the parameter of the 45° direction).
3. The line is broken between 2,0 and 6,0: pieces 0,0–2,0 and 6,0–10,0.

## Actual

1. "60" is read as the distance to the other axis: an ellipse with a 60-unit major axis along Y.
2. The start parameter is atan2(sin45/5, cos45/10) ≈ 63.4°, as if no keyword had been typed.
3. The pieces are 0,0–2,0 and 5,0–10,0 (the break ran from the pick point 5,0 to 2,0), and "6,0" is left over (in a script it is then run at the `Command:` prompt as an unknown command).

title: fix(cmdline): transparent 'ZOOM/'PAN cancel the running command instead of nesting
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Transparent commands that have their own prompts (`'ZOOM`, `'PAN`, `'ZOOM` Window/Object…) cancel the command they are typed in instead of running inside it. `Session::start` only nests transparent commands without an interactive prompt machine; for the others it falls through to `self.cancel()`. It also records the transparent command as the last command, so Enter afterwards repeats ZOOM instead of the interrupted command.

## Steps to reproduce

At the command line (or via `cmdline.input` on the control channel):

```
LINE 0,0
'ZOOM
W
-5,-5
15,15
10,0
```

## Expected

As in AutoCAD: `'ZOOM` runs nested while LINE waits — its prompts are shown with a `>>` prefix — and when it ends, LINE resumes at "Specify next point", so `10,0` draws the segment. Enter at `Command:` afterwards repeats LINE.

## Actual

`'ZOOM` prints `*Cancel*` and ends LINE; the first point is lost, `10,0` is taken as an unknown command, and Enter repeats ZOOM.

title: fix(dwg): saving as DWG loses true colours, transparency, table styles, layout membership and viewport ids
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Saving a drawing as DWG and reopening it loses data that a DXF save keeps. DWG saves go through the DWG bridge: `cadcraft_dwg::dxf_to_dwg` converts our DXF with acadrust, and reading goes acadrust → DXF → our reader. A field-by-field round-trip comparison of synthetic drawings (`write(d, "x.dwg")` → `read`) found these:

- [ ] **True colours become index colours.** An entity with `Color::True(1,2,3)` reopens as ACI 178, and a layer with `Color::True(12,200,99)` as ACI 112. Our DXF says `AC1015`, so acadrust writes an R2000 DWG, and R2000 DWG has no true colour (AC1018 / R2004 added it).
- [ ] **Entity transparency is lost.** A line with transparency 40 % reopens ByLayer. Same cause: R2000 DWG has no entity transparency.
- [ ] **Table styles are lost.** A drawing with table styles `Standard` + `Sched` reopens with only a default `Standard`. R2000 DWG has no TABLESTYLE objects.
- [ ] **Paper-space entities of the second layout move to the first.** A circle on Layout2 reopens on Layout1, and Layout2 is empty. acadrust's R2000 reader can't tell paper-space layouts apart (hakanaktt/acadrust#121, fixed on its `main`, not released yet). AC1018 isn't affected.
- [ ] **A viewport's id changes from 2 to 1, so its model-space view disappears.** DWG doesn't store viewport ids: readers number a layout's viewports in order, and id 1 is the layout's paper-space viewport (the sheet itself). CADCraft keeps that viewport implicit, and MVIEW numbers its viewports from 2, so our files have no id-1 viewport. Through DWG, the first real viewport becomes id 1, and the renderer and layout commands then treat it as the sheet and don't draw it. AutoCAD also takes a layout's first viewport as its paper-space viewport. Separately, our VIEWPORT records lack status group 68 and the always-set bit 32768 of group 90, so acadrust marks them "off".

## Expected

DWG save and reopen keeps true colours, transparency, table styles, layout membership and viewport ids, like DXF does. Plain DX…

title: fix(select): W, C, F, WP and CP selection modes are rejected at Select objects
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

At "Select objects:" only clicks, a two-point window (direction decides window or crossing), `ALL`, `L`/`Last`, `P`/`Previous` and `R`/`A` are understood. The usual typed selection modes are rejected with *Invalid selection*:

- `W` (Window): two corners, objects entirely inside, regardless of the order of the corners
- `C` (Crossing): two corners, objects inside or crossing, regardless of the order
- `F` (Fence): a series of points, Enter ends; objects the fence line crosses
- `WP` / `CP` (Window/Crossing Polygon): a series of points, Enter closes the polygon

This matters most in scripts and for agents driving the command line, where the corner order is the only way to get a window or a crossing.

## Steps to reproduce

Draw three lines: `LINE 0,0 10,0`, `LINE 12,0 20,0`, `LINE 30,0 40,0` (Enter after each), then:

1. `ERASE C 5,-1 25,1` + Enter
2. `ERASE W 25,1 5,-1` + Enter
3. `ERASE F 6,-1 6,1 35,1 35,-1` + Enter + Enter

## Expected

1. Crossing selection: the 0–10 line (crossed) and the 12–20 line (inside) are erased.
2. Window selection: only the 12–20 line (entirely inside) is erased.
3. The fence crosses the 0–10 and 30–40 lines, and both are erased.

## Actual

`C`, `W` and `F` print *Invalid selection*. The points are then taken as an ordinary window whose direction decides the mode: 1 erases only the 12–20 line (a left-to-right window), and 2 erases both the 0–10 and 12–20 lines (a right-to-left crossing). In 3 the points form two zero-width windows and nothing is erased.

title: fix(cmdline): a trailing or double space is not read as Enter in scripts and cmdline input
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

In an AutoCAD script every space ends an input, so a space at the end of a line or two spaces in a row are an Enter. CADCraft loses these Enters:

- `Session::script` calls `trim_end()` on every line, so a trailing space never reaches the command: `ERASE L ` and `JOIN ALL ` stay at "Select objects:".
- `Session::cmdline` (`cmdline.input` on the control channel, MCP) splits the line on any run of whitespace, so the empty input between two spaces disappears: `MOVE L  0,0 5,5` (the double space ends the selection) works in a script but not at the command line, and a trailing space is dropped there too.

## Steps to reproduce

Script (`cadcraft-cli run --script …`, `cmdline.script`):

```
LINE 0,0 5,5

ERASE L 
```
(with a space after `L`)

Command line (`cmdline.input`, one call per line):

```
LINE 0,0 5,5

MOVE L  0,0 5,5
```

## Expected

The script erases the line and returns to `Command:`. The command-line `MOVE` ends the selection at the double space and moves the line to 5,5–10,10, the same as the script path already does.

## Actual

The script stays at `ERASE Select objects:` and the line is not erased. The command-line `MOVE` reads `0,0` and `5,5` as selection points and stays at `MOVE Select objects:`.

title: fix(stretch): selection stops after one window, C is ignored, Displacement does nothing
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

STRETCH does not select the way AutoCAD's does, and its Displacement option does nothing:

- After the first window it goes straight to "Specify base point": "Select objects" is not repeated until Enter, so you can't add a second window or pick more objects.
- Typing `C` (crossing) at the selection prompt is ignored, so the standard script form `STRETCH C <corner> <corner> <Enter> <base> <second>` doesn't work: its points end up as commands.
- Enter at "Specify base point or [Displacement]" ends the command with nothing stretched (AutoCAD takes Displacement as the default there and asks for the displacement).
- The `Displacement` keyword is ignored.
- Enter at "Specify second point or <use first point as displacement>" also ends without stretching.

## Steps to reproduce

Draw a line, then run a script that stretches its right-hand end:

```
LINE 0,0 10,0

STRETCH C 12,1 8,-1  0,0 5,0
```

(two spaces after `8,-1`: Enter ends the selection.)

Also: `STRETCH`, `12,1`, `8,-1`, Enter (base point prompt), `3,4`.

## Expected

The line ends at 15,0 (first case) / 13,4 (second case). "Select objects" repeats until Enter; `C` and `W` choose the window kind; Enter or `D` at the base point asks for a displacement.

## Actual

`C` is ignored, the selection finishes after one window, the command then misreads the following points and the script stops with `Unknown command "0,0"`; the line is not stretched. Enter at the base point ends STRETCH without changing anything.

title: fix(modify): ARRAY is missing; ARRAYRECT/ARRAYPOLAR skip the edit-array option loop
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

The array commands at the command line don't follow the usual prompt sequence:

1. **`ARRAY` doesn't exist.** Typing `ARRAY` (or `AR`) reports "Unknown command". The usual behaviour is: select objects, then "Enter array type [Rectangular/PAth/POlar] <Rectangular>:", then continue as ARRAYRECT, ARRAYPATH or ARRAYPOLAR.
2. **`ARRAYRECT` has no edit loop.** As soon as the selection ends it creates a fixed 4 × 3 grid (spacing 1.5 × the selection size) and ends. You can't set the column/row count or spacing interactively. The usual behaviour is a preview plus a loop: "Select grip to edit array or [ASsociative/Base point/COUnt/Spacing/COLumns/Rows/Levels/eXit] <eXit>:".
3. **`ARRAYPOLAR` only asks for the center and then "Enter number of items".** The edit loop "Select grip to edit array or [ASsociative/Base point/Items/Angle between/Fill angle/ROWs/Levels/ROTate items/eXit] <eXit>:" is missing. Scripts written for that loop break, and the trailing `X` runs EXPLODE.

## Steps to reproduce

Draw a circle, then type each line at the command line (an empty line means Enter):

```
ARRAY
```
→ `Unknown command: ARRAY`

```
ARRAYRECT
L

```
→ the 12-item grid is created at once and the command ends. No COUnt/Spacing/… prompt appears.

```
ARRAYPOLAR
L

0,0
I
4
X
```
→ `I` gives "Requires a positive integer.", `4` creates the array and ends the command, and `X` starts EXPLODE.

## Expected

- `ARRAY`/`AR`: select objects, choose the type, then continue as the chosen array command.
- `ARRAYRECT`: after the selection, a live preview and the edit loop. At least COUnt (columns, then rows), Spacing (columns, then rows), COLumns/Rows (count, then spacing or Total), Base point, and eXit/Enter, which creates the array.
- `ARRAYPOLAR`: "Specify center point of array or [Base point/Axis of rotation]:", then the edit loop with at least Items, Angle between, Fill angle, ROTate items and eXit.
- Options that aren't implemented yet (ASsociative, Levels, …) say so and return to the…

title: fix(inquiry): AREA Object/Add area/Subtract area and DIST Multiple points are silently ignored
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

AREA and DIST list options on the command line that do nothing when chosen: no message, the prompt stays the same, and the input is dropped.

- AREA: `Object`, `Add area` and `Subtract area` at `Specify first corner point or [Object/Add area/Subtract area] <Object>:` are ignored (Enter, the default `Object`, ends the command). There is no way to measure a picked object interactively or to keep a running total.
- AREA: `Arc` and `Length` at `Specify next point` are ignored with fewer than three points, and with three or more they end the command as if `Total` had been chosen.
- DIST: `Multiple points` at `Specify second point or [Multiple points]:` is ignored, so in a script the following points end DIST and the rest of the line is run as commands.

## Steps to reproduce

```
RECTANG 0,0 10,10
AREA
O
10,5
```
Nothing is reported and the prompt is still `Specify first corner point or [Object/Add area/Subtract area] <Object>:`.

```
AREA
A
```
Ignored; the prompt is unchanged.

```
DIST 0,0 M 3,4 3,10
```
DIST reports the distance from 0,0 to 3,4 and ends, then `3,10` is run as a command (`Unknown command`).

## Expected

As AutoCAD's command line does:
- `Object` asks to select an object and reports its area and perimeter.
- `Add area` / `Subtract area` switch to add/subtract mode (`(ADD mode)` / `(SUBTRACT mode)` prompts); each area measured by points or by object is reported and added to or subtracted from a running `Total area = …`. Enter at the first-corner prompt ends the command.
- `Length` at the next-point prompt continues the previous segment by the typed length; options that are not implemented say so ("not available yet") instead of being dropped.
- DIST `Multiple points` takes a series of points, reports the running distance, and Enter (or `Total`) ends it with the total distance.

## Actual

The keywords are silently ignored (or end AREA as `Total`).

title: fix(text): TEXTEDIT prompt says "or or" and ignores Undo/Mode; MTEXT in scripts ends after one line
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Two text commands behave wrongly at the command line and in scripts:

1. TEXTEDIT's prompt reads `Select an annotation object or or [Undo/Mode]:` (doubled "or"), and its `Undo` and `Mode` options are silently ignored.
2. MTEXT in a script (or typed at the command line) takes only the first line of text. The next script line runs as a command, and an empty line repeats MTEXT. On AutoCAD's command line (and in scripts) MTEXT takes one paragraph per line and an empty line ends the text.

## Steps to reproduce

TEXTEDIT:
```
TEXT 0,0 1 0 old

TEXTEDIT
```
Prompt: `TEXTEDIT Select an annotation object or or [Undo/Mode]:`. Pick the text, type `new`, then type `U` at the prompt: nothing happens, the text stays `new`. `M` does nothing either.

MTEXT, as a script:
```
MTEXT 0,10 20,0
First line
Second line

LINE 0,0 5,5

```
## Expected

- TEXTEDIT prompts `Select an annotation object or [Undo/Mode]:`; `Undo` reverts the last edit made in this TEXTEDIT; `Mode` asks for `[Single/Multiple]` and in Single mode TEXTEDIT ends after one edit.
- MTEXT gets one MText with two paragraphs (`First line\PSecond line`), the empty line ends it, and the LINE is drawn.

## Actual

- The doubled "or"; `U`/`M` are dropped.
- MTEXT ends after `First line`; `Second line` is run as a command (`Unknown command "Second"`), and an empty line after an MTEXT repeats MTEXT, which then takes the following input as corners and text.

title: fix(rotate): Reference option is not available and its values run as commands
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

ROTATE offers `Reference` at "Specify rotation angle or [Copy/Reference]", but choosing it only echoes "Reference: not available yet; enter a value.". In a script or one-line command, the reference and new-angle values that follow are then misread, and the leftover tokens run as commands.

## Steps to reproduce

```
LINE 0,0 10,0

ROTATE ALL  0,0 R 30 120
```

## Expected

As in AutoCAD:
1. "Specify the reference angle <0>" takes a typed angle, or two points ("Specify second point").
2. "Specify the new angle or [Points] <0>" takes a typed angle, a point (its angle from the base point), or `P` and two points.
3. The objects turn by the new angle minus the reference angle. Here that is 90°, so the line ends at 0,10.

## Actual

"Reference: not available yet; enter a value." `30` is taken as the rotation angle, and the script then fails with `Unknown command "120"`.

title: fix(draw): SPLINE Close isn't smooth and options are ignored; POLYGON typed-radius orientation; CIRCLE ignores bad input
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Four command-line defects in the SPLINE, POLYGON and CIRCLE prompt sequences:

1. **SPLINE `Close` repeats the first fit point instead of making a smooth closed curve.** The machine appends the first point and fits an open (clamped) spline through it, then sets the closed flag. The result has a corner at the seam, its fit data holds the first point twice, and DXF gets flag 70 = 9 (closed, not periodic). A closed fit-point spline should be periodic: continuous tangent and curvature through the start point, flag 70 bits 1 + 2 (closed + periodic).
2. **SPLINE lists `Method`, `Knots`, `Object`, `start Tangency`, `end Tangency` and `toLerance` but ignores them without a message.** Typing one does nothing and gives no feedback.
3. **POLYGON with a typed radius uses a different orientation in each mode.** Inscribed puts a vertex straight up, so a hexagon or square has a vertex at the bottom. Circumscribed puts a flat edge at the bottom. When the radius is typed, AutoCAD draws the bottom edge horizontal in both modes (at the snap rotation angle). The JSON form defaults to the same vertex-up orientation.
4. **CIRCLE ignores an invalid token at the centre prompt without a message.** Garbage such as `D` gets no response, while LINE and PLINE report `Point or option keyword required.`

## Steps to reproduce

```
SPLINE 0,0 4,0 4,3 0,3 C
```
→ the spline has 5 fit points (0,0 twice), a visible corner at 0,0, and DXF 70 = 9.

```
SPLINE 0,0 T 5,5 L 10,0
```
→ `T` and `L` give no feedback.

```
POLYGON 6 0,0 I 2
POLYGON 6 0,0 C 2
```
→ the inscribed hexagon has a vertex at (0,2) and (0,-2); the circumscribed one has a flat bottom edge.

```
CIRCLE D
```
→ no message; the prompt stays the same.

## Expected

1. A periodic closed spline through the 4 points, smooth at the seam. Fit data stores 4 points, and DXF flag 70 has bits 1 and 2 set.
2. Each option either works or reports that it is not available yet. The command stays at the same prompt and the next token is stil…

title: fix(undo): UNDO doesn't take the number of operations; the number runs as a command
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

UNDO doesn't take a count. It undoes one operation straight away, with no prompt. In a script, the number after it then runs as a command; typed on one line, the number is ignored.

## Steps to reproduce

Draw four circles, then run the script:

```
UNDO 3
```

## Expected

As in AutoCAD, UNDO asks "Enter the number of operations to undo or [Auto/Control/BEgin/End/Mark/Back] <1>:". `3` undoes three operations, and Enter undoes one. U (Edit > Undo, Cmd+Z) still undoes one operation without asking.

## Actual

One circle is undone and the script stops with `Unknown command "3"`.

title: fix(annotate): dimension and multileader options are listed but ignored
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Several dimension and multileader prompts list options that do nothing when chosen: the option is accepted, nothing is reported and the same prompt comes back. In two cases the option does the wrong thing.

## Steps to reproduce
Type at the command line (one line per input):

1. DIMORDINATE: `dimordinate`, `0,0`, `t`, `X=<>`, `10,10` - the text option is accepted but no text prompt appears; the next input is taken as a point and the ordinate becomes a **Y** datum (any keyword other than Xdatum forces Y). `Angle` and `Mtext` do the same.
2. MLEADER: `mleader`, `l` (leader Landing first), `5,5`, `0,0`, `note` - the option is ignored, `5,5` is taken as the arrowhead. `c` (Content first) and `o` (Options) are ignored too, and Enter at the first prompt cancels instead of opening Options.
3. DIMLINEAR / DIMALIGNED: `dimlinear`, `0,0`, `10,0`, `a`, `30`, `5,-3` - "Angle" asks "Specify angle of dimension text" but rotates the dimension **line** by 30 degrees instead of the text.
4. DIMRADIUS / DIMDIAMETER (`Mtext/Text/Angle`), DIMANGULAR (`Mtext/Text/Angle/Quadrant`), DIMARC (`Mtext/Text/Angle/Partial`): every listed option is silently ignored.

## Expected
Each listed option takes effect, as in AutoCAD: Xdatum/Ydatum force the ordinate type, Mtext/Text replace the measured text, Angle rotates the dimension text, Quadrant locks the measured angle to a quadrant, Partial dimensions part of an arc; MLEADER can place the landing or the content first and its Options set leader type, landing, content type, max points and angle constraints (unmodelled choices say "not available yet").

## Actual
The options are ignored (or applied to the wrong thing) with no message.

(DIMLINEAR Horizontal/Vertical/Rotated already work.)

title: fix(modify): OFFSET Erase/Layer/Multiple/Undo and MOVE/COPY Displacement do nothing
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Several options that OFFSET, MOVE and COPY list on their prompts are accepted as keywords but then do nothing:

- **OFFSET `Erase` / `Layer`**: picking either at "Specify offset distance or [Through/Erase/Layer]" is ignored; the prompt just repeats, and the next token is read as the distance. The source is never erased and the offset copy always lands on the source layer.
- **OFFSET `Multiple` / `Undo`**: listed at "Specify point on side to offset or [Exit/Multiple/Undo]" and "Select object to offset or [Exit/Undo]" but ignored.
- **MOVE / COPY `Displacement`**: "Specify base point or [Displacement]" lists it, but `D` (or Enter) does nothing, so the following point is taken as the base point.

## Steps to reproduce

Draw `LINE 0,0 10,0` (then Enter), then:

1. `OFFSET E Y 2 5,0 5,1` then Enter: `E` and `Y` are swallowed (`Y` gives "Requires a positive distance"), the copy is made at y=2 but the source line is kept.
2. `LAYER.NEW {"name":"Other","current":true}`, then `OFFSET L C 2 5,0 5,1` then Enter: the copy is on layer 0, not the current layer `Other`.
3. `OFFSET 2 5,0 M 5,1 5,3` then Enter Enter: `M` is ignored, so `5,3` is read as "select object" and only one copy is made.
4. `MOVE 5,0` Enter `D 3,4`: the line is not moved by (3,4); `3,4` becomes the base point and MOVE waits for a second point. Enter at the base point prompt ends the command. COPY behaves the same.

## Expected

- `Erase` asks "Erase source object after offsetting? [Yes/No]" and `Layer` asks "Enter layer option for offset objects [Current/Source]". Both choices are remembered for the next OFFSET and shown in its "Current settings" line.
- `Multiple` keeps offsetting (each side point offsets the newest copy again) until Enter, which goes back to selecting an object. `Undo` takes back the last offset.
- `Displacement` (or Enter at "Specify base point") asks "Specify displacement" and moves/copies the selection by that vector.

## Actual

All of the keywords above are swallowed with n…

title: fix(insert): -INSERT has no X/Y scale prompts and ignores Basepoint/Scale/Rotate, so script values run as commands
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

The command-line INSERT (`-INSERT`, `INSERT` typed or in a script) doesn't follow the usual prompt sequence, so scripts written for it place blocks wrongly and the leftover values run as commands:

- After the insertion point there is a single "Enter scale factor" prompt instead of an X scale factor prompt followed by a Y scale factor prompt (`<use X scale factor>`). The Y scale is taken as the rotation angle, and the rotation value is then typed at `Command:`.
- The insertion-point prompt lists `[Basepoint/Scale/Rotate]`, but all three keywords are silently ignored, so the values that follow land at the wrong prompts.
- A point picked at the scale prompt is used as a distance (uniform scale), not as the opposite corner that gives the X and Y scale factors.
- The programmatic `insert` only takes a uniform `scale`, so a block can't be inserted with different X and Y scales at all.

## Steps to reproduce

```
LINE 0,0 10,0

-BLOCK B1 0,0 L

-INSERT B1 20,20 1 1 0
-INSERT B1 40,20 2 3 45
-INSERT B1 S 2 60,20 0
-INSERT B1 R 30 80,20 1 1
```

## Expected

- `-INSERT B1 20,20 1 1 0`: X scale 1, Y scale 1, rotation 0.
- `-INSERT B1 40,20 2 3 45`: X scale 2, Y scale 3, rotation 45°.
- `S 2` presets the scale (no scale prompts afterwards); `R 30` presets the rotation (no rotation prompt afterwards); `B` asks for a new base point.

## Actual

- `-INSERT B1 20,20 1 1 0` rotates the block by 1° and then reports `unknown command `0``.
- `-INSERT B1 40,20 2 3 45` inserts at uniform scale 2, rotated 3°, then `unknown command `45``.
- `-INSERT B1 S 2 60,20 0`: `S` and `2` are ignored, `60,20` becomes the insertion point and `0` fails with "Requires a non-zero number."; the command stays at the scale prompt.
- `-INSERT B1 R 30 80,20 1 1`: `R` and `30` are ignored; the second `1` becomes a 1° rotation.

title: fix(modify): FILLET/CHAMFER Trim, Multiple, Undo, Angle, mEthod and Polyline do nothing
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

FILLET and CHAMFER list options on their first prompt that are accepted as keywords but then do nothing:

- FILLET "Select first object or [Undo/Polyline/Radius/Trim/Multiple]": **Trim**, **Multiple** and **Undo** are ignored.
- CHAMFER "Select first line or [Undo/Polyline/Distance/Angle/Trim/mEthod/Multiple]": **Angle**, **mEthod**, **Polyline**, **Trim**, **Multiple** and **Undo** are ignored. The second-line prompt also lists Angle/Method, and they are ignored there too.

## Steps to reproduce

Draw `LINE 0,0 12,0` and `LINE 10,-2 10,12` (each followed by Enter). Then:

1. `FILLET T N R 1 5,0 10,5`: `T` and `N` are swallowed and the lines are trimmed anyway (expected No trim: arc added, lines kept).
2. `FILLET M 5,0 10,5 …`: the command ends after the first fillet. `M` is ignored, so there's no way to fillet several corners in one run, and `U` does nothing.
3. `CHAMFER A 2 45 5,0 10,5`: `A` is ignored, so `2` and `45` are swallowed and the chamfer uses the old distances (expected: 2 along the first line at 45° to it).
4. `CHAMFER E …`: there's no method prompt, so the Distance/Angle method can't be chosen.
5. `PLINE 0,0 10,0 10,10 0,10 C`, then `CHAMFER D 1 1 P 5,0`: `P` is ignored and the pick is taken as the first line.

## Expected

- Trim asks "Enter Trim mode option [Trim/No trim]" and is remembered (TRIMMODE). With No trim, the fillet arc or chamfer line is added and the source objects are left alone.
- Multiple repeats the first/second selection until Enter. Undo (within the command) takes back the last fillet or chamfer.
- CHAMFER Angle asks for a chamfer length on the first line and an angle from it (CHAMFERC/CHAMFERD, CHAMMODE=1). mEthod asks "Enter trim method [Distance/Angle]". Polyline chamfers every corner of a 2D polyline, as FILLET Polyline already does.

## Actual

All of the keywords above are swallowed with no effect.

title: fix(block): redefining a block with its own reference makes it reference itself and loses its geometry
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Redefining a block with a selection that contains a reference to that same block (directly, or through another block that contains it) is accepted. The block then references itself, and its original geometry is gone. Every existing reference draws only the new objects plus a reference to itself, which nests until the depth limit. The cycle is also written to saved files. AutoCAD refuses such a definition ("references itself") and leaves the drawing unchanged.

In the same path, redefining a block with a name that differs only in case (`Door` and then `DOOR`) creates a second block instead of redefining the first. Block names are case-insensitive, and name lookups pick one of the two arbitrarily.

## Steps to reproduce

Self-reference (command line):

```
LINE 0,0 10,0

-BLOCK B 0,0 L

LINE 0,0 0,10

-BLOCK B 0,0 ALL

```

The second `-BLOCK` selects the converted reference of `B` and the new line.

Through a nested block (JSON):

```
line {"points":[[0,0],[10,0]]}
block {"name":"A","base":[0,0]}          (selection: the line → reference of A)
line {"points":[[0,0],[0,10]]}
block {"name":"B","base":[0,0]}          (selection: reference of A + line → reference of B)
block {"name":"A","base":[0,0],"handles":[<reference of B>]}
```

Case:

```
block {"name":"Door","base":[0,0],"handles":[<a line>]}
block {"name":"DOOR","base":[0,0],"handles":[<another line>]}
blocks.list {}
```

## Expected

- The redefinition is refused with a "Block "B" references itself" message. Block `B` keeps its line, and the selected objects stay as they were.
- `DOOR` redefines `Door`, so there is one block.

## Actual

- `Block "B" defined with 2 object(s).` `B` now holds a reference to `B` and the vertical line. The original horizontal line is lost from the definition.
- In the nested case, `A` holds a reference to `B`, which holds a reference to `A`.
- `blocks.list` shows both `DOOR` and `Door`.

title: fix(layer): -LAYER has no command-line form; scripts cannot create or set layers
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

`-LAYER` has no command-line form. The dash is stripped and `-layer` resolves to the `layer` listing command, which runs at once and ends. Every following token is then read as a new command, so scripts cannot create a layer, make it current or change its properties.

## Steps to reproduce

Script (or one command-line entry):

```
-LAYER M Walls C 1 Walls 
```

## Expected

The AutoCAD-style option loop: `Enter an option [?/Make/Set/New/Rename/ON/OFF/Color/Ltype/LWeight/TRansparency/MATerial/Plot/Freeze/Thaw/LOck/Unlock/stAte/Description/rEconcile]:`. Here `M Walls` creates layer Walls and makes it current, `C 1 Walls` makes it red, and Enter ends the command. The changes are one undo step. Invalid values are rejected, for example a linetype that is not loaded.

## Actual

`Command: LAYER` lists the layers and ends. `M` then starts MOVE, `Walls` is an unknown command, and so on. No layer is created.

Related: `layer.set` / `layer.new` accept a linetype that is not loaded in the drawing, and `layer.set {newName}` can rename a layer to the name of another existing layer, which leaves two layers with the same name.

title: fix(render): nested, self-referencing or arrayed block references in a DXF hang the app
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Opening a small DXF whose block references multiply (a block that inserts itself a few times, a chain of blocks that each insert the next several times, or one MINSERT with large row/column counts) makes CADCraft hang and eat memory. `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH` (16) bounds the recursion *depth*, but nothing bounds the total number of block copies expanded: a block that references itself 4 times expands to 4^16 ≈ 4·10⁹ copies, and an MINSERT is clamped to 10,000 × 10,000 = 10⁸ copies per reference.

Two places expand block references without a total budget:

- `cadcraft_render::build` (`insert()` in `crates/render/src/lib.rs`): drawing the model / exporting PNG, SVG, PDF.
- `cadcraft_doc::entity_bounds` (`crates/doc/src/extents.rs`): drawing extents, which also runs when saving a DXF (`$EXTMIN/$EXTMAX`), for ZOOM Extents, `cadcraft-cli info`, and the spatial index.

A fuzzed 2.8 KB DXF (blocks inserting each other a few times) produced 28.7 million display primitives (37 s in a debug build) and 4 s for its extents.

## Steps to reproduce

`selfref.dxf` (227 bytes): block `A` holds a line and four references to itself; model space holds one `A`.

2. `cadcraft-cli convert selfref.dxf out.png`. It doesn't finish within 30 s.

4. Opening either file in the app hangs it the same way.

## Expected

A hostile or broken file opens quickly (never crash, never hang). Like cyclic references, block expansion has a limit: past a bo…

title: fix(render): model-space linetypes in layout viewports ignore PSLTSCALE (dashes shrink with the viewport scale)
author: vangel76

title: fix(render): points ignore PDMODE/PDSIZE, so the Point Style setting has no visible effect
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Point objects ignore `PDMODE` and `PDSIZE`. Format ▸ Point Style… (`ddptype`) stores both variables, but the renderer always draws a POINT as a one-pixel dot. Choosing X, +, tick, circle or square has no effect on the canvas, in Plot Preview or in PNG/SVG/PDF exports. Users normally change the point style to see the points that POINT, DIVIDE and MEASURE place, and in CADCraft those points stay nearly invisible.

## Steps to reproduce

```json
{"command":"point","params":{"at":[5,5]}}
{"command":"ddptype","params":{"pdmode":35,"pdsize":1.0}}
```

(`PDMODE` 35 = X inside a circle, `PDSIZE` 1 = one drawing unit.) Look at the drawing, or export it with `cadcraft_io::write(d, "out.svg")` / PDF.

## Expected

The point draws as an X with a circle around it, one drawing unit across, as the Point Style dialog shows. `PDMODE` 1 draws nothing, and +32 / +64 add a circle / square. A negative `PDSIZE` is a percentage of the view height, and 0 means 5 %.

## Actual

`PDMODE` = 35 and `PDSIZE` = 1 are stored, but the display list holds a single `Kind::Point` for the point and the SVG has a single dot (`<circle r=…>` the hairline size). Every `PDMODE` value draws the same.

title: fix(purge): -PURGE has no prompts; it purges everything and the rest of the line runs as commands
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

`-PURGE` (and `PURGE`) has no prompts. It purges every unused block, layer and linetype immediately, and the rest of the line or script then runs as commands. A script cannot purge only one kind of object, choose names, or answer the usual verify question.

The JSON form has related problems:
- `purge` takes no parameters, so purging only layers is impossible. Purging always deletes unused blocks too.
- The params doc says `{} (unused blocks, layers, linetypes, styles)`, but no styles are ever purged.
- A linetype used only inside a block definition, or set as the current linetype (CELTYPE), counts as unused and is purged.

## Steps to reproduce

Script:

```
-PURGE A * N
```

and

```
-PURGE LA * N
```

## Expected

AutoCAD-style prompts:
1. `Enter type of unused objects to purge [Blocks/DEtailviewstyles/Dimstyles/Groups/LAyers/LTypes/MAterials/MUltileaderstyles/Plotstyles/SHapes/textSTyles/Mlinestyles/SEctionviewstyles/Tablestyles/Visualstyles/Regapps/Zero-length geometry/Empty text objects/Orphaned data/All]:`
2. `Enter name(s) to purge <*>:`
3. `Verify each name to be purged? [Yes/No] <Y>:` For No, everything matching is purged without asking. For Yes, each name is confirmed one at a time.

`LA` purges only unused layers. Object types CADCraft does not have report that there is nothing to purge.

## Actual

`Command: PURGE` prints `0 blocks, 0 layers, 0 linetypes purged.` and ends. Then `A` starts ARC and `*` is an unknown command. `-PURGE LA` also deletes unused blocks.

title: fix(rename): RENAME has no command-line form and cannot rename blocks
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

RENAME / -RENAME has no command-line form, and the JSON form cannot rename blocks even though the params doc lists `block`.

- Typed `RENAME` or `-RENAME` runs the JSON form with no parameters and fails with "`from` is required". Every following token then runs as a command.
- `rename {"table": "block", ...}` returns "unsupported table", although the params doc says `{table: layer|linetype|style|dimstyle|block, from, to}`. There is no other way to rename a block.

## Steps to reproduce

Script:

```
-RENAME LA Old New
```

JSON:

```
rename {"table": "block", "from": "Valve", "to": "Valve-2"}
```

## Expected

- The AutoCAD-style prompts `Enter object type to rename [Block/Dimstyle/LAyer/LType/Material/multileadeRstyle/Plotstyle/textStyle/Tablestyle/Ucs/VIew/VPort]:`, then `Enter old layer name:`, then `Enter new layer name:`. The rename goes through the same engine command as the JSON form.
- Block rename renames the definition and re-points every INSERT that uses it: in model space, in layouts, nested inside other block definitions, and inserts that carry attributes. Arrowhead references in dimension styles are updated too. A new name that matches an existing block case-insensitively, an invalid name, or an anonymous block is rejected.

## Actual

`invalid parameters for rename: from is required`, and `unsupported table` for blocks.

title: fix(spline): programmatic SPLINE accepts any degree, and a high degree hangs the app
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

The programmatic SPLINE command (`spline {"control": [...], "degree": N}`) accepts any degree up to the number of control points minus one. A spline with a few thousand control points and a high degree then takes minutes to tessellate. Its extents, drawing and every redraw (zoom, pan, selection) hang the app.

SPLINE at the command line (`Degree` option), `spline.cv` and the DXF reader all limit the degree to 1–10, as in AutoCAD. Only this JSON path (`run_spline` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/draw.rs`) skips the limit.

Found by fuzzing `Session::execute` with hostile parameters.

## Steps to reproduce

Control channel / MCP / `cadcraft-cli run --cmd`, with 3000 control points (any coordinates):

```
spline {"control": [[x0,y0], [x1,y1], ... 3000 points ...], "degree": 2147483647}
```

Measured in a debug build, with the extents computed after the command (as the app does for the redraw):

| degree | time |
|---|---|
| 3 | 10 ms |
| 1000 | 5 s |
| 2147483647 (clamped to 2999) | 65 s |

The spline is created with degree 2999, and every later redraw takes as long again.

## Expected

The degree is limited to 1–10, as for SPLINE's `Degree` option, `spline.cv` and DXF input.

## Actual

The degree is limited only by the number of control points, and tessellation and extents grow roughly with its square, so the app hangs.

title: fix(render): PNG export panics in debug builds when a point lands mid-pixel
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

PNG export (and anything else that uses the CPU rasteriser in `crates/render/src/raster.rs`, such as the plot preview and MCP/agent screenshots) panics in debug builds when a POINT lands at certain sub-pixel positions. Points are drawn as a 1.5 px anti-aliased square with `Pixmap::fill_rect`; tiny-skia's anti-aliased rectangle filler hits a `debug_assert!(false)` (`scan/hairline_aa.rs:124`) when a rectangle narrower than two pixels has both its left and right edges inside adjacent pixels (e.g. left = 12.3, right = 13.8). Release builds skip the assertion and draw correctly, but dev builds, `cargo test` and debug CLI builds crash, which breaks the never-crash rule.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a debug build, create a drawing with a line from `0,0` to `10,7` and a point: `POINT` → `3,0`.
2. Export it to a 2400 × 1600 PNG (`cadcraft_io::png(&d, &Space::Model, 2400, 1600)`, or the PNG export command / tool).

Any point whose screen x coordinate has a fractional part above about one half triggers it, so a drawing with a handful of points crashes almost always.

## Expected

The PNG is written, with the point drawn as a small dot.

## Actual

`thread panicked at tiny-skia-0.11.4/src/scan/hairline_aa.rs:124:21: assertion failed: false`

title: fix(render): near-white and near-black colours flip with the background, not just colour 7
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

`cadcraft_color::display_rgb` (used by the canvas, the GPU mesh, PNG/raster, PDF and SVG export) flips **any** colour whose luminance is above 0.94 to black on a light background, and any colour below 0.06 to white on a dark one. Only colour 7 (directly, or reached through ByLayer/ByBlock) should behave that way: it means "white or black, whichever contrasts with the background". Every other index or true colour should keep its RGB.

What goes wrong today:
- On white paper (PDF, SVG): ACI 51 (light yellow, 255,255,127), ACI 255 (white) and true-colour 255,255,255 all print black. White solid hatches used to mask parts of a drawing print as black blocks.
- On the dark canvas and in PNG export: the dark index colours (luminance < 0.06, e.g. 18, 28, 168, 178, 188, 198, 208, 218, 228, 238, 248) and true-colour black show as white.

## Steps to reproduce

Through `engine.execute` (JSON form):

1. `{"command":"color","params":{"color":51}}`, then `{"command":"line","params":{"points":[[0,0],[10,0]]}}` (a light-yellow line).
2. `{"command":"color","params":{"color":"255,255,255"}}`, then `{"command":"line","params":{"points":[[0,2],[10,2]]}}` (a true-colour white line; a white SOLID hatch behaves the same).
3. `{"command":"color","params":{"color":250}}`, then `{"command":"line","params":{"points":[[0,4],[10,4]]}}` (a dark-grey line).
4. Export to PDF or SVG, then look at the model-space canvas or a PNG export.

## Expected

The colour-51 line prints light yellow and the white fill stays white (so it masks) on paper. Colour 250 is dark grey on the dark canvas. Only colour-7 / ByLayer-on-a-colour-7-layer geometry is black on paper and white on the dark canvas.

## Actual

The colour-51 line and the white fill print black on paper. The dark index colours show as white on the dark canvas and in PNG.

title: fix(attedit): ATTEDIT typed at the command line fails with "`handle` is required"; -ATTEDIT missing
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
ATTEDIT (and its aliases ATE / EATTEDIT) has no command-line prompt sequence. Typed at the command line it runs the JSON form with no parameters and fails at once, so a block's attribute values cannot be edited from the command line or a script. -ATTEDIT (the command-line attribute editor with block/tag/value filters and global find/replace) is not available either.

## Steps to reproduce
```
attdef {"tag":"T","default":"one","at":[0,0]}
line 0,0 10,0
block B 0,0 all

insert {"name":"B","at":[0,0]}
attedit
```

## Expected
`Select block reference:` then, for each attribute of the picked block, `Enter value for T <one>:` (Enter keeps the current value); the new values are applied as one undo step. `-ATTEDIT` asks `Edit attributes one at a time? [Yes/No] <Y>:` and the block name / tag / value specifications, then edits the matching attributes one at a time or replaces a string in all of them.

## Actual
```
Command: ATTEDIT
invalid parameters for `attedit`: `handle` is required
```
`-attedit` behaves the same.

title: fix(attedit): attribute tags match case-sensitively in INSERT/ATTEDIT values and unknown tags are silently ignored
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Attribute tags are matched case-sensitively by the JSON forms of INSERT (`attribs`) and ATTEDIT (`values`). Tags are case-insensitive in AutoCAD (ATTDEF stores them in upper case), so `{"t": "x"}` for tag `T` should set it. Instead the value is silently dropped: INSERT uses the default, ATTEDIT reports `changed: 0`, and neither says which tags did not match.

## Steps to reproduce
```
attdef {"tag":"T","default":"one","at":[0,0]}
line 0,0 10,0
block B 0,0 all

insert {"name":"B","at":[0,0],"attribs":{"t":"two"}}
attedit {"handle":"<handle from above>","values":{"t":"three"}}
attedit {"handle":"<handle from above>","values":{"NOPE":"x"}}
```

## Expected
INSERT sets T to `two`; ATTEDIT sets T to `three` and returns `changed: 1`. A tag the block does not have is reported in the result (e.g. `unknownTags: ["NOPE"]`).

## Actual
INSERT leaves T at `one`; ATTEDIT returns `{"changed":0}` and leaves T unchanged; the unknown tag `NOPE` is ignored without a word.

title: fix(blocks): ATTDISP is missing and the display ignores ATTMODE
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
ATTDISP (attribute display: Normal / ON / OFF, stored in the ATTMODE system variable) does not exist, and the display ignores ATTMODE: invisible attributes are always hidden and visible ones always shown.

## Steps to reproduce
```
attdisp
setvar {"name":"ATTMODE","value":2}
```
(with a block reference that has an invisible attribute, e.g. `attdef {"tag":"H","default":"hidden","at":[0,0],"invisible":true}`, `line 0,0 10,0`, `block B 0,0 all`, `insert {"name":"B","at":[0,0]}`)

## Expected
`ATTDISP` prompts `Enter attribute visibility setting [Normal/ON/OFF] <Normal>:` and sets ATTMODE to 1 / 2 / 0. With ON (2) invisible attributes are drawn too; with OFF (0) no attributes are drawn; Normal (1) draws only the visible ones.

## Actual
``unknown command `attdisp` ``. Setting the ATTMODE header variable (e.g. `setvar {"name":"ATTMODE","value":2}`) changes nothing on screen or in plots.

title: fix(blocks): ATTSYNC is missing
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
ATTSYNC does not exist. After a block is redefined with added, removed or moved attribute definitions, the existing block references keep their old attributes and there is no way to bring them up to date.

## Steps to reproduce
```
attdef {"tag":"A","default":"a","at":[0,0]}
line 0,0 10,0
block B 0,0 all
insert {"name":"B","at":[0,0],"attribs":{"A":"kept"}}
; redefine B with a new attribute C and without A ... then
attsync
```

## Expected
`Enter an option [?/Name/Select] <Select>:`; with a block chosen (by name or by picking one of its references), every reference of that block gets the block's current attribute definitions: missing attributes are added with their default values, attributes whose definition is gone are removed, existing values are kept for matching tags, and position/height/style/visibility follow the definition.

## Actual
``unknown command `attsync` ``.

title: fix(annotate): DIMCONTINUE/DIMBASELINE take quadratic time on long point lists
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

`dimcontinue` / `dimbaseline` with a long `points` list take time that grows quadratically with the list length. 4,000 points take about 0.25 s, 16,000 take 2.7 s (continue) and 10 s (baseline), and 50,000 points take well over 8 s. The app stays frozen for that time. There is also no limit on the number of points per call.

The cause: with DIMASSOC on (the default), every new dimension looks for the object under each definition point with `assoc::find_snap`, which scans the whole space. The chain adds one dimension per point, so the space grows by one entity per point, and the total work is points × entities. With `DIMASSOC 0` the same 16,000-point chain takes about 40 ms.

## Steps to reproduce

```
dimlinear {"p1":[0,0],"p2":[1,0],"at":[0,2]}
dimcontinue {"points":[[2,0],[3,0],[4,0], ... 16000 points ...]}
```

Do the same with `dimbaseline`.

## Expected

The time grows roughly linearly with the number of points. An absurdly large input is refused with a clear message, not processed.

## Actual

The time grows quadratically, and a 50,000-point call freezes the app for many seconds.

title: fix(engine): begin/prompt/preview of interactive commands are not under the catch_unwind guard
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

The last-resort `catch_unwind` guard (AGENTS.md, "Never crash") covers `Session::execute` and interactive input (`run.machine.input` in `Session::feed`). It does not cover the other steps of an interactive command:

- the command's machine factory and `Running.machine.begin`, the first step of `Session::start` (`feed(None)`);
- `machine.prompt()`, called by `current_prompt()` and `prompt_text()`, which the UI calls every frame and the session calls before every input;
- `machine.preview()`, called by `Session::preview` for the rubber band on every cursor move.

A panic in any of these escapes to the caller and takes down the app, losing the drawing. `prompt` and `preview` are worse than input: they run on every frame, not once per typed value.

## Steps to reproduce

This is a code-level gap; any bug in a machine's `begin`/`prompt`/`preview` triggers it. For example, a machine whose `preview` indexes past the end of a vector panics on the first mouse move after the command starts. The panic is not caught, unlike the same bug in `input`.

## Expected

As for `execute` and `input`: the drawing is restored, the command ends with "Internal error in <command>: …", and the app keeps running.

## Actual

The panic unwinds out of `Session::start` / `current_prompt` / `prompt_text` / `preview`.

title: fix(layer): LAYMRG and LAYDEL are missing (merge layers, delete a layer with its objects)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

The layer tools LAYMRG (merge layers) and LAYDEL (delete a layer together with its objects) don't exist. Typing either one at the command line or in a script fails with an unknown-command error, and a script stops there. The only way to remove a layer that still has objects is to erase every object by hand (model space, every layout, every block definition) and then call `layer.delete`.

(LAYWALK is the third layer tool from the same menu. It is a dialog-only browser, so it is out of scope here.)

## Steps to reproduce

```
layer.new {"name":"A","current":true}
LINE 0,0 10,0

layer.current {"name":"0"}
LAYMRG
N
A

N
0
Y
```

and

```
layer.new {"name":"B","current":true}
LINE 0,5 10,5

layer.current {"name":"0"}
LAYDEL
N
B

Y
```

## Expected

- **LAYMRG**: "Select object on layer to merge or [Name]:" repeats until Enter (Name types a layer name, Undo removes the last one). Then "Select object on target layer or [Name]:", a warning naming the layers, and "Do you wish to continue? [Yes/No] <No>:". On Yes, every object on the source layers (model space, layouts and inside block definitions) moves to the target layer. Viewport per-layer freezes and colour overrides of the source layers are dropped, and the source layers are deleted. Merging a layer into itself is refused, and so is a source of layer 0, Defpoints or an xref-dependent layer. When the current layer is merged away, the target becomes current.
- **LAYDEL**: "Select object on layer to delete or [Name]:" repeats until Enter, then a warning and the same Yes/No confirmation. On Yes, the layer and every object on it (model space, layouts and inside block definitions) are deleted. Layer 0, Defpoints, the current layer and xref-dependent layers are refused.
- JSON forms that never prompt: `laymrg {"from": [names], "to": name}` and `laydel {"names": [...]}`.

## Actual

``unknown command `LAYMRG` `` / ``unknown command `LAYDEL` ``; nothing changes.

title: fix(render): hatch island style, background colour and gradient colours are ignored when drawing
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Three hatch properties that CADCraft already stores are ignored when a hatch is drawn (canvas, PNG/SVG/PDF export, plot):

1. **Island detection style** (`Hatch::style`, DXF group 75: 0 normal, 1 outer, 2 ignore) has no effect. Every hatch is filled with odd parity, so an *outer* hatch still fills the island-within-an-island and an *ignore* hatch still leaves the islands empty.
2. **Background colour** of a pattern hatch (`Hatch::background`, kept since #215) is never drawn: only the pattern lines appear.
3. **Gradients** are drawn as a flat fill in `color1` only: `color2`, the gradient name (LINEAR, CYLINDER, SPHERICAL, …), the angle and the centred/shifted flag are ignored. A `ByLayer` (or `ByBlock` with no block colour) `color1` comes out white instead of the layer colour, because the gradient colour is resolved against colour 7 instead of the hatch's layer.

## Steps to reproduce

Gradient (command line / control channel):

```
LAYER M Red C 1 Red <Enter>
RECTANG 0,0 10,10
{"command":"gradient","params":{"points":[[5,5]],"color1":"bylayer","color2":"3"}}
```
then export: `cadcraft-cli run --script ... --export out.png` (or look at the canvas).

Island style and background: open a DXF holding a pattern HATCH with three nested square loops (0..10, 2..8, 4..6), group `75` = 1 (or 2), and a background colour in the hatch's `CADCRAFT` xdata (as written by our own DXF writer), then export to PNG.
