title: fix(dxf): custom hatch pattern definitions are dropped on read and save; unknown patterns draw as ANSI31
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

A DXF HATCH carries its pattern's definition lines (groups 78 count, then per line 53 angle, 43/44 base point, 45/46 offset, 79 dash count and 49 dash lengths). CADCraft skips them on read and keeps only the pattern name. Any pattern that isn't in CADCraft's own library (a custom pattern, or a standard name CADCraft doesn't define) is therefore drawn as ANSI31. On save the definition is lost for good: the writer writes `78 0` because it finds no library pattern with that name.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Make a DXF holding a HATCH with pattern name `MYGRID` and two definition lines (0° and 90° lines, offset 0,1, no dashes) around a 10×10 square.
2. `cadcraft-cli run <file.dxf> --export out.png` → diagonal ANSI31 lines instead of a grid.
3. Open the DXF and save it again; the saved HATCH has `78` = 0, so other programs can't draw the pattern either.

## Expected

The definition lines are kept in the drawing (for patterns not in the library), drawn when the name isn't in the library, and written back on save. Hostile counts (huge 78 / 79 values, non-finite numbers) are capped or skipped and never panic.

## Actual

Drawn as ANSI31; the definition is dropped on save.

title: fix(render): wipeouts don't mask — objects behind them stay visible on screen and in PNG/SVG/PDF
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
A WIPEOUT does not hide anything: it is drawn only as its frame polygon, so objects behind it stay visible on the canvas and in PNG, SVG and PDF output. A wipeout should cover what is drawn before it (draw order) with the background colour — paper white when plotting/exporting to SVG/PDF, the canvas background on screen — and draw its frame only as `WIPEOUTFRAME` says (0 = no frame, 1 = displayed and plotted, 2 = displayed but not plotted).

(Not the same as #79 / #147, which were about *saving* wipeouts to DXF.)

## Steps to reproduce
```
LINE 0,0 10,10
WIPEOUT 2,2 8,2 8,8 2,8

WIPEOUT F OFF
```
then export PNG / SVG / PDF (e.g. `cadcraft-cli run --script ... --export out.png`) or look at the canvas.

## Expected
The diagonal line is hidden inside the square (the square is filled with the background colour); with `WIPEOUT F OFF` the square's outline is not drawn either. `DRAWORDER` (Bring to Front) on the line brings it back on top of the wipeout.

## Actual
The diagonal line runs through the square; the square is only an outline, and the outline stays visible with frames OFF.

title: fix(render): "Default" lineweight is always 0.25 mm; LWDEFAULT is ignored
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Objects whose lineweight resolves to "Default" are always drawn and plotted at 0.25 mm. The `LWDEFAULT` system variable (the width "Default" stands for) is ignored.

## Steps to reproduce
```
SETVAR LWDEFAULT 70
LINE 0,0 100,0

```
then turn on lineweight display (`LWDISPLAY 1`) or plot to PDF.

## Expected
The line (lineweight ByLayer → layer 0 → Default) is drawn at 0.70 mm, as with a 0.70 mm lineweight.

## Actual
It is drawn at 0.25 mm whatever `LWDEFAULT` says (`crates/render/src/lib.rs` hard-codes 0.25 for Default).

title: fix(render): wide (filled) polylines ignore their linetype
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
A polyline with width (constant or tapered) is always filled as one continuous band; its linetype is ignored. CAD programs dash wide polylines too: each dash is a filled piece of the band and the gaps are empty (PLINEGEN decides whether the pattern runs per segment or along the whole polyline, as for thin polylines).

## Steps to reproduce
Load DASHED and make it current (JSON form: `{"command":"linetype","params":{"load":"DASHED","current":"DASHED"}}`, or Format ▸ Linetype), then at the command line
```
PLINE 0,0 W 0.2 0.2 10,0

```
and look at the canvas / export PNG.

## Expected
A row of filled 0.2-wide dashes with gaps.

## Actual
One continuous filled band; the linetype only shows when FILLMODE is 0.

title: fix(linetype): library linetypes use inch dash lengths in metric drawings
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Linetypes loaded from CADCraft's library always use inch dash lengths, also in metric drawings. In a metric drawing (MEASUREMENT 1, mm) with LTSCALE 1 the DASHED dash is 0.5 mm long, so dashed lines look continuous unless the user finds and sets LTSCALE ≈ 25. CAD programs load metric-scaled definitions for metric drawings (MEASUREMENT = 1 uses the ISO-scaled linetype file, where the same linetypes have their lengths multiplied by 25.4), so LTSCALE 1 looks right in both unit systems.

## Steps to reproduce
New metric drawing, load DASHED and make it current (`{"command":"linetype","params":{"load":"DASHED","current":"DASHED"}}`), then
```
LINE 0,0 100,0

```

## Expected
Dashes about 12.7 mm long with 6.35 mm gaps at LTSCALE 1 (the pattern scaled for millimetres).

## Actual
0.5 mm dashes with 0.25 mm gaps — the line looks solid.

title: fix(blocks): WBLOCK ignores base when writing a block by name
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

`wblock` takes `base` (the insertion base point of the written drawing), but ignores it when `name` (write a block) is given. The block's own base point is always used, so you can't write a block with another insertion point.

## Steps to reproduce

```
line {"points": [[10, 20], [15, 20]]}
block {"name": "Part", "base": [4, 4], "handles": ["<the line's handle>"], "keep": "delete"}
wblock {"path": "/tmp/part.dxf", "name": "Part", "base": [10, 20]}
```

Then open `/tmp/part.dxf` (or INSERT it at 0,0).

## Expected

The written drawing has its base point, the origin and `$INSBASE` 0,0,0, at the requested point (10,20 in the block's coordinates), so the line starts at 0,0. This is how the objects form (`handles` + `base`) already works.

## Actual

`base` is ignored: the line starts at 6,16, measured from the block's own base point 4,4.

title: fix(theme): System pins the native macOS window appearance
author: coygeek
body:

title: fix(modify): OFFSET of a closed spline produces an open spline
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
OFFSET of a closed spline creates an **open** spline. The offset copy is rebuilt with the open (clamped) fit-point interpolation, so it has `closed: false`, a clamped knot vector and a tangent break where the original curve starts. AutoCAD offsets a closed spline to a closed spline. The closed (periodic) interpolation exists since #240 (`Spline::from_fit(fit, closed)`), but OFFSET doesn't use it yet.

## Steps to reproduce
```
SPLINE 0,0 10,0 10,10 0,10 C
OFFSET 1 <pick the spline> 5,5
LIST <pick the new spline>
```
(or `engine.execute("offset", {"handle": <spline>, "distance": 1, "side": [5,5]})`)

## Expected
The offset copy is a closed spline (periodic, like the original), smooth at the start point. Commands that need a closed boundary (HATCH, REGION, AREA Object, …) accept it.

## Actual
The offset copy is open (`closed: false`, clamped knots). It starts and ends at the same point, but it is not closed and has a corner at the seam.

title: fix(blocks): -BLOCK converts the selection instead of erasing it, and redefines without asking
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
The command-line `-BLOCK` doesn't behave like AutoCAD's `-BLOCK`:

1. **The selection is converted to a block reference instead of being erased.** AutoCAD's `-BLOCK` removes the selected objects from the drawing once the block is defined. (The BLOCK *dialog* is where you choose Retain / Convert to block / Delete.) In CADCraft, `-BLOCK` is just an alias of `BLOCK` and always converts. So a script that runs `-BLOCK` and then `INSERT`s the block ends up with an extra reference at the base point.
2. **No redefinition question.** When the name is already in use, AutoCAD asks `Block "<name>" already exists. Redefine it? [Yes/No] <N>:`. CADCraft replaces the existing definition without asking, which also changes every reference to it.

Behaviour that stays as it is: the JSON form `block {name, base, handles, keep}` (default `keep: "convert"`) and the Draw ▸ Block ▸ Make... path keep converting the selection.

## Steps to reproduce
```
LINE 0,0 10,0

-BLOCK B 0,0 L

INSERT B 20,0 1 0
```
Then:
```
LINE 0,0 0,10

-BLOCK B 0,0 L

```

## Expected
- After the first `-BLOCK`, the line is erased and the drawing is empty. After `INSERT`, there is exactly one reference to B.
- The second `-BLOCK B` asks `Block "B" already exists. Redefine it? [Yes/No] <N>:`. `N` or Enter goes back to the block name prompt. `Y` continues with the base point and selection, then redefines B.

## Actual
- After the first `-BLOCK`, the line has been replaced by a reference to B at 0,0, so after `INSERT` there are two references.
- The second `-BLOCK B` silently replaces B's definition.

title: fix(render): text in complex linetypes (FENCELINE1, GAS-style) is never drawn
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Linetypes with embedded text (the built-in FENCELINE1, or GAS/HW-style linetypes read from a DXF; since #216 their text elements survive DXF round trips) draw only their dashes. The text element is treated as part of the gap, so a "gas line" shows `----    ----    ----` instead of `---- GAS ---- GAS ----`. Shape elements (from SHX shape files) are not drawn either.

## Steps to reproduce

Control channel / MCP (`engine.execute`), then the command line:

```
{"command":"linetype","params":{"load":"FENCELINE1","current":"FENCELINE1"}}
LINE 0,0 10,0
```

(or open a DXF whose LTYPE has a `74 = 2` text element and draw a line with it), then look at the canvas or export a PNG.

## Expected

At every repeat of the pattern the embedded text is drawn in its text style, at its size (`46`, times the style's fixed height when it has one, times the linetype scale), rotated relative to the line direction (or absolutely, `74` bit 1), shifted by its X/Y offsets along and across the line, starting where the element that carries it ends — like any CAD program shows complex linetypes.

## Actual

Only the dashes are drawn; the text never appears (on screen, PNG, SVG or PDF).

Shapes need SHX shape files, which CADCraft doesn't read; they can keep drawing nothing, but that should be documented.

title: fix(snap): object snaps ignore geometry inside block references
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Object snaps ignore the geometry inside block references. Hovering over a line, arc or circle that belongs to an inserted block offers only the block's **Insertion** point; Endpoint, Midpoint, Center, Quadrant, Intersection, Perpendicular, Tangent and Nearest never find anything inside the block. In practice you can't snap to doors, fixtures, title-block frames, or anything else that comes in as a block, which includes most real DWG/DXF drawings.

The cause is in `crates/engine/src/snap.rs`: `osnap` collects candidates from `EntityKind::prims()`, and for an `INSERT` that returns only the insertion point. The renderer expands blocks, but snapping never does.

## Steps to reproduce

Command line, OSNAP Endpoint/Midpoint/Center on:

```
LINE 0,0 10,0

CIRCLE 20,0 2
-BLOCK B 0,0 ALL

```

then insert it scaled by 2 and rotated 30°. The JSON form avoids the `-INSERT` prompt issue #245:

```json
{"command": "insert", "params": {"name": "B", "at": [100, 100], "scale": 2, "rotation": 30}}
```

Then hover near the right end of the inserted line, at about `117.32,110`, or near the circle's centre at about `134.64,120`.

At engine level: `snap::osnap(doc, &Space::Model, p, 0.5, mode::END | mode::MID | mode::CEN, None, false)` near those points returns `None`.

## Expected

Snaps find the block's geometry where it is drawn, with the reference's position, rotation, scale and mirroring applied. That includes non-uniform scale, which turns a circle into an ellipse. Nested references and MINSERT arrays work too, as in AutoCAD. Insertion also snaps to visible attributes.

## Actual

Only the block's insertion point snaps (Insertion). Nothing else inside the block can be snapped to.

title: fonts: CRAFT_FONTS_DIR is documented and packaged but never embedded
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

AGENTS.md says fonts live in [storytold/craft-fonts](https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts) and are "an optional build input (`CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`)". `NOTICE`, `packaging/env.sh`, `packaging/macos/package.sh` and `packaging/windows/package.ps1` say builds made with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` **embed** its fonts and ship their OFL licences. But no Rust code reads `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`, so:

- a build made with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` set embeds nothing, yet its packages ship `OFL-<family>.txt` licences for fonts that aren't in the binary;
- the app never gets the craft-fonts fonts. This matters most on the web build, which has no system fonts: Japanese or Arabic text in a drawing has no font at all there and is drawn as missing-glyph boxes.

The other Crafting Apps follow craft-fonts' `docs/integration.md`: a `build.rs` reads `$CRAFT_FONTS_DIR/fonts/manifest.txt` and generates `CRAFT_FONTS: &[CraftFont]` with `include_bytes!` (see pdfcraft `crates/fonts/build.rs`, photocraft `crates/text/build.rs`). If the variable is unset, the slice is empty and nothing changes.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts ../craft-fonts
git grep CRAFT_FONTS_DIR -- '*.rs'          # nothing
CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=$PWD/../craft-fonts cargo build --release -p cadcraft-cli
```

Then, in a drawing with no Japanese font installed (or in the web build): `TEXT` → `0,0` → `2.5` → `0` → `日本語`.

## Expected

With `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` set, the craft-fonts fonts are compiled in and used. They can be named as text-style fonts (e.g. `BIZ UDPGothic`), and they are the fallback for characters the text's font lacks. On web builds that means the UI face (BIZ UDPGothic Regular) and the Arabic face only, as in the sibling apps. Without the variable the build stays as it is.

## Actual

The binary is the same with or without `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`. The text is drawn as boxes unless a system font covers it, and the package still ships the font licences.

## Notes

- AGENTS.md bars Adobe fo…

title: fix(grips): grip stretch and grip Move/Rotate/Scale/Mirror ignore the other selected objects
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Grip editing only changes the one object whose grip was clicked, even when several objects are selected:

- **Stretch:** two selected lines share a corner. Dragging the corner grip moves only one line's endpoint, so the lines come apart. In AutoCAD every selected object with a grip at that point stretches with it, and connected geometry stays connected.
- **Move, Rotate, Scale and Mirror** (Space/Enter cycles through them on a hot grip): only the clicked grip's object is transformed. In AutoCAD these modes act on the whole selection, about the hot grip.

The cause is `Session::grip_edit` in `crates/engine/src/grips.rs`. It always sends `handles: [handle]` to `grip.move`/`grip.rotate`/`grip.scale`/`grip.mirror`, and `grip.move` in stretch mode (`stretch` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/gripcmds.rs`) edits a single object.

## Steps to reproduce

```
LINE 0,0 10,0 10,10

```

1. Select both segments with a window.
2. Click the grip at `10,0` and click `12,3`.
3. Select both segments again, click the grip at `0,0`, press Space once (Move) and click `1,1`.

At engine level: `s.set_selection(vec![a, b]); s.grip_edit(a, 2, Vec2::new(12.0, 3.0), GripMode::Stretch)` leaves `b` starting at `10,0`.

## Expected

- Step 2: both segments meet at `12,3`.
- Step 3: both segments move by `1,1`.

## Actual

- Step 2: only the first segment's end moves, leaving a gap at the corner.
- Step 3: only the first segment moves.

title: fix(snap): Nearest snap prefers a circle over a closer object (depends on drawing order)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

The Nearest object snap (NEA) does not always pick the closest point. When a circle lies within the aperture, its nearest point replaces any earlier candidate, even when that candidate is closer to the cursor. Which point you get depends on the order the objects were drawn in.

## Steps to reproduce

```
LINE -5,0 5,0
(Enter)
CIRCLE 0,3.8 3
OSMODE 512
LINE
```

At "Specify first point", hover the cursor at about (0, 0.1) with an aperture that reaches both objects. The line is 0.1 away and the circle's edge (0, 0.8) is 0.7 away.

Engine level: `snap::osnap(doc, &Space::Model, Vec2::new(0.0, 0.1), 1.0, mode::NEA, None, false)`.

## Expected

The marker and the snapped point land on the line at (0, 0), the closest point of any object in the aperture, whatever the drawing order.

## Actual

The point snaps to the circle at (0, 0.8). If the circle is drawn before the line, the same cursor position snaps to the line instead.

Cause: in `osnap_with` (crates/engine/src/snap.rs), the `Prim::Circle` branch of the Nearest search assigns `nb` without comparing its distance to the best candidate so far.

title: fix(cmdline): typed angles ignore ANGBASE, ANGDIR and AUNITS
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Typed angles ignore the drawing's angle settings. Polar input (`@d<a`, `d<a`) and every angle typed at a prompt (TEXT/INSERT/RECTANG rotation, XLINE Ang, ROTATE, ARC included angle, polar ARRAY angles, LENGTHEN, HATCH, DIMLINEAR Rotated, …) all go through `units::parse_angle`. That function always reads a bare number as decimal degrees, measured counterclockwise from +X:

- **ANGBASE** (the direction of angle 0) and **ANGDIR** (1 = clockwise) are ignored.
- **AUNITS** is ignored, so in a radians (3) or grads (2) drawing, `@10<1.5708` is read as 1.57°.

Related: `SETVAR ANGBASE 90` stores 90 as is, but the header and `$ANGBASE` in DXF hold the base angle in radians, as in DWG/ODA. A file written by another program round-trips, but values typed through SETVAR are wrong.

## Steps to reproduce

```
SETVAR ANGBASE 1.5707963267948966
SETVAR ANGDIR 1
LINE 0,0 @10<90
(Enter)
SETVAR AUNITS 3
LINE 0,0 @10<1.5707963267948966
(Enter)
```

## Expected

- With 0 = north and clockwise angles, `@10<90` points east, so the first line ends at (10, 0).
- With AUNITS 3, a bare number is in radians, so the second line ends at (0, 10).
- Explicit units still work in any AUNITS: `90d`, `45d30'15"`, `1.5708r`, `100g`, `N45dE`.
- The AutoCAD-style overrides `d<<a` (degrees) and `d<<<a` (current units) measure from +X counterclockwise, bypassing ANGBASE and ANGDIR.
- ROTATE turns clockwise for positive angles when ANGDIR is 1.
- JSON params keep their documented meaning, unaffected by these settings.

## Actual

- The first line ends at (0, 10).
- The second line ends at (9.996, 0.274), because 1.5708 was read as degrees.
- `<<` is not understood.

title: fix(file): Save As to .png/.svg/.pdf renames the drawing to the image and marks it saved, so unsaved work is lost on close
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Saving to an image or PDF path with SAVEAS (or QSAVE with a `path`) writes the export, but then treats it as a save of the drawing. The drawing is renamed to the image file, and its unsaved-changes state is cleared, although no DXF/DWG was written. As a result:

- Closing the drawing or quitting no longer asks "Save changes?", so the drawing is lost.
- A later Save (QSAVE / Ctrl+S, MCP `save {}`, control `app.save {}`) exports the PNG/SVG/PDF again instead of saving the drawing.

There are several ways to get here:
- the desktop Save As dialog offers SVG, PNG and PDF filters;
- the MCP `save` tool documents ".svg/.png export by extension";
- the control channel's `app.save {path}`;
- `saveas {"path": …}` from scripts.

The code already says otherwise in one place: `save_reporting` and the `save_reports_not_saved` test treat an image export as "not a save of the drawing". But `commit_save` (crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs) sets `saved`, `path` and `title` for every extension.

## Steps to reproduce

Headless MCP (`cadcraft-cli mcp`):

```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"command_line","arguments":{"text":"circle 0,0 5"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"save","arguments":{"path":"/tmp/p2.png"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"inspect_drawing","arguments":{"entities":false}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"save","arguments":{}}}
```

Desktop: draw a circle, then File > Save As…, choose the PNG filter and save as `p2.png`. Then close the drawing.

## Expected

The PNG is written. The drawing keeps its name (`Drawing1`) and its unsaved changes, as with AutoCAD's image export commands, which don't rename the drawing. Closing still asks to save. A later Save without a path still asks for, or needs, a drawing file name.

## Actual

- Reply 3: `"title": "p2.png"`, `"path": "/tmp/p2.png"`, `"dirty": false`.
- Reply 4 writes `/tmp/p2.png` …

title: fix(snap): elliptical arcs and splines have no Midpoint, Perpendicular or Tangent snaps; Quadrant snaps off an elliptical arc
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Object snaps on ellipses, elliptical arcs and splines are incomplete (`crates/engine/src/snap.rs`):

- **Midpoint** never snaps on an elliptical arc or an open spline (only lines and circular arcs have one).
- **Quadrant** on an elliptical arc offers all four quadrant points of the full ellipse, including the ones that are not on the arc.
- **Perpendicular** and **Tangent** from a base point only work on lines, circles and circular arcs; an ellipse, elliptical arc or spline gives neither.

## Steps to reproduce
1. `ELLIPSE` `A` `C` `0,0` `4,0` `2` `0` `90` (a quarter of an ellipse from (4,0) to (0,2)).
2. `SPLINE` through `0,0` `3,4` `6,0` `9,4`, Enter.
3. `OSMODE` `2` (Midpoint only), `LINE` and hover the middle of the elliptical arc or of the spline.
4. `OSMODE` `16` (Quadrant only), `LINE` and hover (-4,0) or (0,-2).
5. `OSMODE` `384` (Perpendicular + Tangent), `LINE` `10,10`, then hover the ellipse arc or the spline where a line from (10,10) would meet it at a right angle or touch it.

## Expected
As in AutoCAD: Midpoint snaps to the point halfway along the length of an elliptical arc or spline; Quadrant only snaps to quadrant points that lie on the arc; Perpendicular snaps to the foot points of the normals from the base point, and Tangent to the points where a line from the base point touches the curve (each solution offered, the one nearest the cursor wins, as for circles).

## Actual
No Midpoint marker on the elliptical arc or the spline; Quadrant snaps to (-4,0) and (0,-2) although the arc does not pass there; no Perpendicular or Tangent marker on the ellipse arc or spline.

title: fix(snap): dimensions have no snaps, justified DXF text snaps and grips at the wrong point, grid snap ignores SNAPBASE/SNAPANG, hatches snap without OSNAPHATCH
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Several object-snap and grid-snap details differ from AutoCAD (`crates/engine/src/snap.rs`, grid snap in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`):

1. **Dimensions have no snaps.** AutoCAD snaps into a dimension's (block) geometry: Endpoint on the ends of the dimension and extension lines, Node on the definition points. CADCraft offers nothing on a dimension (only Nearest on nothing; the definition point is not even a Node).
2. **Insertion snap and grip of justified TEXT read from DXF use the wrong point.** For a TEXT with a justification other than Left (or Left with a vertical alignment), the insertion point is the alignment point (DXF group 11). CADCraft's Insertion snap and the text's grip use group 10 (the computed left baseline point) instead. Text created in CADCraft is not affected (both points coincide).
3. **Grid snap ignores SNAPBASE and SNAPANG.** The snap grid always starts at 0,0 and runs along the axes; there is no SNAPBASE or SNAPANG.
4. **Hatch boundaries snap.** AutoCAD ignores hatch objects for object snaps while OSNAPHATCH is 0 (its default); CADCraft snaps to the hatch boundary's ends, midpoints and intersections, and has no OSNAPHATCH.

## Steps to reproduce
1. `DIMLINEAR` `0,0` `10,0` `5,3`, then `OSMODE` `9` (Endpoint + Node) and start `LINE`; hover the top end of an extension line, the end of the dimension line at (10,3), or the definition point (0,0) with no other object there.
2. Open a DXF with a right-justified TEXT: group 72 = 2, group 10 = (0,0), group 11 = (10,0). `OSMODE` `64`, `LINE`, hover (10,0); select the text and look at its grip.
3. `SNAPMODE` `1`, `SNAPUNIT` `1,1`, `SETVAR` `SNAPBASE` `0.5,0.5` (or `SNAPANG` `45`), then `LINE` and move the cursor.
4. `RECTANG` `0,0` `10,5`, `HATCH` it, `ERASE` the rectangle; `OSMODE` `1`, `LINE`, hover (10,5).

## Expected
1. Endpoint snaps on the dimension and extension line ends; Node snaps on the definition points.
2. The Insertion snap and the grip are at (10,0), the point the text is j…

title: fix(mcp): malformed tool arguments are ignored (query_entities returns everything, command_line presses Enter), unknown tools and empty batches aren't JSON-RPC errors
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Several MCP tool calls are accepted with arguments that don't fit the tool's input schema, and the server guesses instead of reporting an error. An agent then gets a plausible-looking but wrong answer (every entity, an Enter keypress) and keeps going.

- `query_entities` ignores a malformed `window` (a flat `[x0,y0,x1,y1]`, a single point, an object) and non-string `type`/`layer`, and returns **every** entity. Its `count` is the size of the returned page, not the number of matches, so an agent can't tell that results were cut off by `limit` (and `offset` is accepted by the engine but missing from the tool schema). The window test is a bounding-box overlap, so a circle or arc that only has its bounding box over the window matches.
- `command_line` with a missing or non-string `text` (`{}`, `{"cmd": "erase all"}`, `{"text": 5}`) or non-object `arguments` (`"circle 1,1 1"`) presses **Enter**, which repeats the last command.
- `script` without `text` runs an empty script and reports success.
- An unknown tool name returns a normal result with `isError: true` instead of the JSON-RPC error `-32602` that the MCP spec (2025-06-18, *Error Handling*) uses for unknown tools and invalid arguments.
- An empty batch `[]` gets no reply at all; JSON-RPC 2.0 requires a single Invalid Request (`-32600`) response.
- `list_commands {"filter": "circle"}` matches the filter anywhere in the command's JSON (parameter docs, menus), so it returns QSELECT, CENTERMARK, DIMRADIUS, … next to CIRCLE.

## Steps to reproduce

`cadcraft-cli mcp`, then send these lines (after `initialize`):

```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"command_line","arguments":{"text":"circle 0,0 1"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"command_line","arguments":{"text":"circle 100,100 1"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"query_entities","arguments":{"window":[-5,-5,5,5]}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","…

title: fix(modify): MOVE/SCALE/ROTATE/ARRAY/OFFSET… can overflow to infinite coordinates; the object shows null and DXF save moves it to 0,0
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Every input to MOVE, COPY, SCALE, ROTATE, MIRROR, ARRAY, STRETCH, OFFSET (and grip edits) is checked for being finite, but the **result** isn't. Finite inputs can still overflow: moving a circle by `[1e308, 1e308]` twice puts its centre at infinity. Nothing reports a problem. The object then shows `null` coordinates in `drawing.inspect`, the drawing extents become `null`, and saving to DXF writes the centre as `0.0`, so the geometry silently changes on save and reopen.

The same happens typed at the command line (`MOVE`, `0,0`, `1e308,1e308`, twice).

## Steps to reproduce

JSON (`cadcraft-cli mcp`, `execute`, or the control channel's `engine.execute`):

```
execute {"command": "circle", "params": {"center": [0, 0], "radius": 1}}
execute {"command": "move", "params": {"handles": ["100"], "delta": [1e308, 1e308]}}
execute {"command": "move", "params": {"handles": ["100"], "delta": [1e308, 1e308]}}
inspect_drawing {}
save {"path": "/tmp/x.dxf"}
open {"path": "/tmp/x.dxf"}
inspect_drawing {}
```

Command line (as a script, one input per line, blank line = Enter):

```
CIRCLE 0,0 1
MOVE
ALL

0,0
1e308,1e308
MOVE
ALL

0,0
1e308,1e308
```

Other ways to get there from a far-out object: `scale` with factor `1e308`, `rotate` by 180° about `[-1e308, -1e308]`, `arrayrect` with `rowSpacing: 1e308`, `offset` by `1e308`.

## Expected

The second MOVE fails with a clear message ("the result is too large…") and the drawing and undo history stay as they were, so the circle is still at 1e308,1e308. The same goes for the other commands.

## Actual

The second MOVE reports `{"moved": 1}`. `inspect_drawing` shows `"center": {"x": null, "y": null}` and `"extents": [[null, null], [null, null]]`. The saved DXF has the circle at `0,0`, so after reopening it sits at the origin.

title: fix(insert): -INSERT can't insert exploded (*name) or insert a drawing file
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
`-INSERT` only accepts the name of a block already defined in the drawing. Two common command-line forms are missing:

- **`*name` — insert exploded.** AutoCAD inserts the block's contents as individual objects; it then asks for one (uniform) scale factor and the rotation, and no attribute values.
- **Inserting a drawing file.** `-INSERT C:\path\part.dxf` (or `part=C:\path\part.dwg`) defines a block named after the file (or after the part before `=`) from the file's model space — taking along the layers, linetypes, styles and blocks it needs and keeping the definitions this drawing already has — with the file's `$INSBASE` as the base point, then inserts it. The JSON form has no way to insert a file either.

Today both forms print `Block "…" not found.` and stay at the name prompt, so in a script every following value (the insertion point, scale, rotation) is read as another block name.

## Steps to reproduce
```
-INSERT B1 0,0 1 1 0      (B1 an existing block — works)
-INSERT *B1 10,0 1 0
-INSERT C:\parts\bolt.dxf 0,0 1 1 0
```
or `engine.execute insert {"file": "/parts/bolt.dxf", "at": [0, 0]}`.

## Expected
- `-INSERT *B1 10,0 1 0` adds B1's objects at 10,0 (scale 1, rotation 0) as separate objects, no block reference.
- `-INSERT C:\parts\bolt.dxf 0,0 1 1 0` defines block `bolt` from the file (base point = the file's INSBASE) and inserts it; `bolt=C:\parts\bolt.dxf` redefines `bolt` from the file; `*C:\parts\bolt.dxf` inserts its contents exploded.
- JSON: `insert {file, name?, at, …}` does the same without any dialog; `name: "*B1"` inserts exploded.

## Actual
`Block "*B1" not found.` / `Block "C:\parts\bolt.dxf" not found.`, then `Block "10,0" not found.`, `Block "1" not found.` … The command never inserts anything. The JSON form requires `name` and has no `file` parameter.

title: fix(text): TL/ML/BL text from DXF is drawn, measured and picked one offset away from its alignment point
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Single-line TEXT with **Left** horizontal justification and a vertical alignment (TL, ML, BL: DXF group 72 = 0 with group 73 = 3, 2 or 1) read from a DXF file is drawn one alignment offset too low (TL, ML) or too high (BL). Its extents (zoom, window selection) and picking box are off by the same amount.

The DXF Reference says group 11 (second alignment point) is the meaningful point for every justification other than baseline-left. Group 10 (first alignment point) is then a computed point on the baseline at the text's left end. The renderer (`cadcraft_fonts::place`) and `text_box` in `crates/doc/src/extents.rs` place Center/Right/Middle text from group 11, but Left text always from group 10, and then shift it again by the vertical alignment. For TL that puts the top of the text one text height below the alignment point.

Text drawn with CADCraft's own TEXT command doesn't show the problem: it stores the same point in both fields.

## Steps to reproduce
Open a DXF with this TEXT (height 1, TL):
```
  0
TEXT
  8
0
 10
0.0
 20
-1.0
 40
1.0
  1
TOP
 72
0
 11
0.0
 21
0.0
 73
3
```
(or build the same `Text` with `insert = (0,-1)`, `align_pt = (0,0)`, `halign Left`, `valign Top` and call `render::place_text_entity` / `doc::entity_bounds`).

## Expected
The top-left of "TOP" is at 0,0 (the alignment point). The text occupies y from -1 to 0, and its extents and pick box match.

## Actual
The text is drawn with its top at y = -1 (rendered box y -2.33 … -1.0). Extents and picking report the same wrong box. ML and BL are off by half a text height and by a third of a text height respectively.

title: fix(json): draw and annotation commands accept negative/zero sizes and coincident points, creating degenerate objects
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

The JSON forms of several draw and annotation commands (`engine.execute`, MCP, scripts using the JSON form) accept invalid sizes and coincident points. Some values are silently made absolute or clamped, others create degenerate objects. The command reports success, so an agent cannot tell that its input was wrong.

Related: #85 (zero-radius ARC, fixed) and #84 (MTEXT height, fixed) covered one parameter each. This is the same problem in the other commands.

## Steps to reproduce

Each line is one `engine.execute` call (`{"command": …, "params": …}`) on an empty drawing (for HATCH, a closed 10×10 rectangle exists):

```

circle   {"center":[0,0],"diameter":-2}                     -> circle with radius 1
circle   {"center":[0,0],"radius":1e-300}                   -> circle with radius 1e-300
arc      {"center":[0,0],"radius":-5,"start":0,"end":90}    -> arc with radius 5
polygon  {"sides":-3,"center":[0,0],"radius":5}             -> square (sides silently become 4)
polygon  {"sides":6,"center":[0,0],"radius":0}              -> 6 vertices all at 0,0
polygon  {"sides":6,"center":[0,0],"radius":-5}             -> hexagon (rotated)
polygon  {"sides":6,"edge":[[0,0],[0,0]]}                   -> 6 vertices all at 0,0
donut    {"center":[0,0],"inside":-1,"outside":2}           -> donut from |inside|
donut    {"center":[0,0],"inside":0,"outside":0}            -> zero-size polyline
donut    {"center":[0,0],"inside":5,"outside":2}            -> donut (inside > outside)
rectang  {"p1":[0,0],"p2":[10,5],"fillet":-1}               -> plain rectangle, no message

rectang  {"p1":[0,0],"p2":[10,5],"width":-1}                -> width 0, no message
pline    {"vertices":[[0,0],[1,0]],"width":-1}              -> width 0, no message
pline    {"vertices":[{"p":[0,0],"startWidth":-1},[1,0]]}   -> stores start…

title: fix(control): a timed-out control request still runs later, so a retry applies it twice
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

The control server (`apps/cadcraft/src/control_server.rs`) waits 60 s for the app to answer a request, then replies `{"ok": false, "error": "timeout"}`. The request is still in the app's queue, though. When the UI thread gets to it (after a long command, a modal file dialog, a stalled frame…) it runs it anyway and the result is thrown away. A client that retries after the timeout applies the change twice, for example two circles from one `engine.execute circle`. The client also cannot tell whether a timed-out request ran at all.

This is the server-side twin of #102, which #146 fixed for the MCP bridge's lost replies.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `cadcraft --control 7777`
2. Keep the UI thread busy for more than 60 s (a long-running command, or a window that presents no frames so `drain_control` doesn't run).
3. Send `{"id":1,"method":"engine.execute","params":{"command":"circle","params":{"center":[0,0],"radius":5}}}`. After 60 s the reply is `{"id":1,"ok":false,"error":"timeout"}`.
4. Retry the same request, as a client reasonably does after a timeout.
5. When the app catches up, `drawing.inspect` shows two circles.

## Expected

A timed-out request that the app has not started is cancelled and never runs. The reply says so: `{"ok": false, "error": "timeout", "state": "not-run"}`, so a retry is safe. If the app had already started the request when the server gave up, the reply says `"state": "may-have-run"`, so the client inspects the drawing before retrying.

## Actual

The reply is a bare `"timeout"`, and the queued request runs later anyway.

title: fix(io): DWG reopen loses ANGBASE/ANGDIR/FILLETRAD/CHAMFERA/B/ELEVATION/THICKNESS; SNAPBASE/SNAPANG never saved
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Some drawing settings are lost when a drawing is saved and reopened:

- **Through DWG only:** `ANGBASE`, `ANGDIR`, `FILLETRAD`, `CHAMFERA`, `CHAMFERB`, `ELEVATION` and `THICKNESS` come back as 0. The DWG file holds them. acadrust reads them into its document, but its DXF writer (0.6.3, also current `main`) leaves them out of the HEADER section. Our DWG reader goes DWG → acadrust → DXF → our reader, so they never arrive.
- **Through DXF and DWG:** the snap grid's origin and rotation (`SNAPBASE`, `SNAPANG`, which grid snap has followed since #337) are never saved. Since R13 they live in the `*ACTIVE` VPORT record (groups 13/23 and 50), not in the header. Our writer always writes snap base 0,0 and no rotation, and our reader ignores the VPORT table.

Checked and fine through DWG: `AUNITS`, `AUPREC`, `LUNITS`, `LUPREC`, `INSUNITS`, `MEASUREMENT`, `LTSCALE`, `DIMSCALE`, `PDMODE`, `PDSIZE`, `TEXTSIZE`, `CELTSCALE`, `PSLTSCALE`, `LWDISPLAY`, `ORTHOMODE`, `MIRRTEXT`.

(`LWDEFAULT` isn't saved either, but AutoCAD keeps it as a per-user setting, not in the drawing, so that matches.)

## Steps to reproduce

At the command line:

```
SETVAR ANGBASE 90
SETVAR ANGDIR 1
FILLET R 2
SAVEAS /tmp/a.dwg
OPEN /tmp/a.dwg
SETVAR ANGBASE
```

Or in code: set those header variables on a `Drawing`, then `cadcraft_io::write(&d, "x.dwg")` followed by `cadcraft_io::read(&bytes, "x.dwg")`. For the snap grid, set `SNAPBASE` 3,4 and `SNAPANG` 30, then round-trip through DXF.

## Expected

The angle base, angle direction, fillet radius, chamfer distances, elevation, thickness and snap grid origin and rotation are the same after reopening.

## Actual

`ANGBASE` reads 0 and `ANGDIR` reads 0 (counterclockwise). The fillet radius, chamfer distances, elevation and thickness read 0, and the snap grid is back at 0,0 with no rotation.

title: fix(control): headless and app replies differ for cmdline.input, command-line state and app.open
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

The app's control channel (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`) and the headless MCP backend (`cadcraft-cli mcp`, `crates/mcp/src/backend.rs`) serve the same methods, but they reply differently. A client written against one breaks against the other:

- **`cmdline.input` with a refused line** (for example an unknown command): headless puts the message in an `error` field, and `output` stays empty because the message isn't added to the history. The app echoes the message into `output` and the history, and has no `error` field. To tell that a line failed, a client has to check `error` on one backend and parse `output` on the other.
- **Command-line state** (`cmdline.state`, `cmdline.key`, `cmdline.input`): the app returns `accept`, `buffer` and `historyExpanded`; headless doesn't return them.
- **`app.open` without `path`**: the app answers `missing path` itself. Headless passes `{"path": null}` to the OPEN command, which fails with a message about `path` or `data`, but `app.open` never forwards `data`.

## Steps to reproduce

Headless, `cadcraft-cli mcp`, through the `command_line` tool (control method `cmdline.input`):

```
{"text": "nosuchcommand"}
```

Then the same against the app (`cargo run -p cadcraft -- --control 9876`):

```
{"id":1,"method":"cmdline.input","params":{"text":"nosuchcommand"}}
{"id":2,"method":"cmdline.state","params":{}}
{"id":3,"method":"app.open","params":{}}
```

## Expected

Both backends reply with the same fields and the same errors, documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`.

## Actual

- Headless `cmdline.input`: `{"output": [], "error": "...", "prompt": ..., "running": ..., "keywords": ..., "history": [...]}`.
- App `cmdline.input`: `{"output": ["..."], "prompt": ..., "running": ..., "keywords": ..., "accept": ..., "buffer": ..., "history": [...], "historyExpanded": ...}`.
- Headless `app.open {}` fails with the OPEN command's error. The app fails with `missing path`.

title: fix(cmdline): ROTATE, HATCH, dimension and CHAMFER/MLEADER angle prompts ignore AUNITS, ANGBASE and ANGDIR
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

#326 / #328 made typed angles follow the drawing's angle settings (AUNITS for bare numbers, ANGBASE as angle 0, ANGDIR 1 = clockwise). A few angle prompts still use `units::parse_angle`, which always reads decimal degrees counterclockwise from +X. #328 left them for after the PRs that rewrote them. Those PRs (#247, #251) have now merged.

- ROTATE: "Specify rotation angle"
- HATCH / -HATCH: "Specify an angle for the hatch pattern"
- DIMLINEAR / DIMALIGNED Rotated: "Specify angle of dimension line"
- Dimension Angle text option (DIMLINEAR, DIMANGULAR, DIMARC, DIMORDINATE, …): "Specify angle of dimension text"
- MLEADER Options: "Enter first/second angle constraint"
- CHAMFER Angle: "Specify chamfer angle from the first line"

Several of these prompts already show their default in AUNITS, such as the ROTATE, HATCH and CHAMFER defaults. So in a radians drawing the prompt offers `0.7854r`, while typing `0.7854` means 0.79°.

## Steps to reproduce

```
SETVAR AUNITS 3
LINE 0,0 10,0
(Enter)
ROTATE ALL (Enter) 0,0 1.5707963267948966
```

Also, with `SETVAR ANGDIR 1` (and AUNITS 0), `ROTATE ALL (Enter) 0,0 90` turns the line counterclockwise.

## Expected

The angles are read like every other typed angle:
- **Amount** (bare number in AUNITS): CHAMFER angle, MLEADER angle constraints.
- **Rotation** (AUNITS, turned clockwise when ANGDIR is 1; ANGBASE does not apply): the ROTATE angle (as #326 says, "ROTATE turns clockwise for positive angles when ANGDIR is 1"). Also the hatch pattern angle, which AutoCAD measures from the UCS X axis rather than from ANGBASE.
- **Direction** (measured from ANGBASE in the ANGDIR sense): the dimension line angle (Rotated) and the dimension text angle.

The first ROTATE gives a line ending at (0, 10). With ANGDIR 1, the second turns the line clockwise to (0, -10).

## Actual

The first line ends at (9.996, 0.274), because the value was read as 1.57°. With ANGDIR 1 the line turns counterclockwise to (0, 10).

title: fix(annotate): QDIM scans the whole drawing for every dimension it adds (quadratic) and has no input cap
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

QDIM looks up the objects under each new dimension's definition points by scanning the whole drawing (`add_dim` → `assoc::reassociate`), once per dimension it adds. Each dimension adds an entity, so a QDIM over many objects takes quadratic time. It also has no cap on the input size. This is the same problem #279 fixed for DIMCONTINUE/DIMBASELINE (PR #281).

## Steps to reproduce

Over the control channel or MCP (DIMASSOC = 2, the default):

```
engine.execute line {"points": [[0,0],[1,0],[2,0], … ,[20000,0]]}      (20,000 lines)
engine.execute qdim {"handles": [<the 20,000 line handles>], "at": [0,3]}
```

## Expected

QDIM finishes in about the same time as DIMCONTINUE with the same number of points, and a call that would add more than 100,000 dimensions or name more than 100,000 objects is refused before anything is created, as DIMCONTINUE/DIMBASELINE do.

## Actual

The QDIM call takes about 28 s in a debug build (the time grows with the square of the number of dimensions). There is no input cap, so a single polyline with a few hundred thousand vertices keeps the engine busy for a very long time.

title: fix(blocks): an attribute's own layer, colour, linetype and lineweight are lost; -ATTEDIT Layer/Color not available
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

An attribute (ATTRIB) is an entity with its own layer, colour, linetype and lineweight. AutoCAD copies them from the attribute definition on insertion, and they can then be changed on one attribute alone, for example with -ATTEDIT Layer/Color or in another program. CADCraft's `Attrib` has no fields for them, which causes three problems:

- **DXF reading loses them.** An ATTRIB's groups 8/62/420/370/6 are ignored, so the attribute is drawn with its ATTDEF's properties (#313).
- **DXF writing replaces them.** Every ATTRIB is written on its block reference's layer, without colour, linetype or lineweight. Other programs then show attributes defined on another layer, or with a colour, differently from CADCraft.
- **-ATTEDIT can't set them.** The Layer and Color options (one attribute at a time) only say "not available yet".

## Steps to reproduce

```
ATTDEF (tag T, default one) at 0,1, BLOCK B with it, INSERT B at 100,0
-LAYER N A (Enter)
-ATTEDIT Y (Enter) T (Enter) 105,0 (Enter)
L
```

Also: open a DXF whose INSERT has an ATTRIB with `62` = 1 (red) while its ATTDEF is ByLayer.

## Expected

- -ATTEDIT Layer asks for an existing layer name and Color for a colour (name, number, Truecolor `r,g,b`). Each applies to that attribute only, and the attribute is drawn with it.
- Reading a DXF keeps an ATTRIB's own layer, colour, linetype and lineweight. Writing gives each ATTRIB the properties it is drawn with, so reopening, and other programs, show the same.
- ATTSYNC resets these per-attribute changes to the definitions. AutoCAD's ATTSYNC documentation notes that it removes format and property changes made with ATTEDIT/EATTEDIT.

## Actual

- `L` answers "Layer is not available yet." (Color: "Color is not available yet.")
- The red ATTRIB is drawn ByLayer, and saving writes it without a colour.

title: fix(control): cmdline.key Enter errors: headless fails the call, the app drops the error
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

`cmdline.key` with `{"key": "enter"}` replies differently in the app and headless when Enter is refused. Headless (`cadcraft-cli mcp`) fails the call with `{"ok": false, "error": …}`. The app's control channel ignores the error: it replies `"ok": true` with the plain state, and nothing reaches the history. Pressing Enter in the app's command line does echo the error. This is a follow-up to #351 / #352, which aligned `cmdline.input` (a refused line is echoed to the history and `output`, `error` only when refused, the call itself succeeds). `cmdline.key` also replies without `output` in both, so a caller can't see what Enter or Escape printed (`*Cancel*`, a repeated command's messages).

## Steps to reproduce

Over the control channel (`cadcraft --sample --control PORT`) and headless (`cadcraft-cli mcp`, same methods):

```
{"id":1,"method":"cmdline.input","params":{"text":"close"}}
{"id":2,"method":"cmdline.key","params":{"key":"enter"}}
```

Enter repeats CLOSE, which needs an open drawing.

## Expected

Both reply `"ok": true` with the command-line state, `output` (the lines the key added, including the error), and `error` ("command `close` is not available right now: no drawing open"). The error is also in `history`, as when Enter is pressed in the command line. Without an error there is no `error` field.

## Actual

- Headless: `{"ok": false, "error": "command `close` is not available right now: no drawing open"}`.
- App: `{"ok": true, "result": {…state…}}`. The error is dropped and isn't in the history.
- Neither reply has `output`.

title: fix(annotate): MLEADER forgets the placement order and Options for the next run
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

MLEADER forgets the placement order (leader arrowhead first / leader landing first / content first) and the values set at its Options prompt (Maxpoints, leader landing, content type, first and second angle) as soon as the command ends. The next MLEADER starts again with "arrowhead first" and the defaults. AutoCAD keeps these choices for the next MLEADER in the session, so drawing a series of leaders the same way doesn't require re-entering the order and options each time. The options themselves came in #247 (#243).

## Steps to reproduce

```
MLEADER
L                      (leader Landing first)
O M 3 A N X            (Options: Maxpoints 3, no landing line, eXit)
10,5 5,5 0,0 one
MLEADER
```

## Expected

The second MLEADER asks "Specify leader landing location or [leader arrowHead first/Content first/Options] <Options>:" and draws a three-point leader with no landing line. Choosing another order or other options changes what the next MLEADER uses. JSON `engine.execute mleader` keeps its documented defaults.

## Actual

The second MLEADER asks "Specify leader arrowhead location or [leader Landing first/Content first/Options] <Options>:", with Maxpoints 2 and a landing line.

title: fix(annotate): DIMBASELINE spacing ignores SETVAR DIMSCALE/DIMDLI overrides, and DIMSCALE 0 stacks baseline dimensions on one line
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

DIMBASELINE places each new dimension line `DIMDLI` drawing units above the previous one using only the base style's own `DIMDLI` and `DIMSCALE`. It ignores the dimension's overrides and the drawing's DIMSCALE. Since #129, `SETVAR DIMSCALE` / `SETVAR DIMDLI` are stored as overrides on new dimensions, so they have no effect on baseline spacing. A scaled drawing therefore gets baseline dimensions 0.38 units apart while their text is 10× larger, and the dimensions overlap.

A style whose DIMSCALE is 0 ("scale to layout", which the renderer falls back to the drawing's DIMSCALE for) gives a spacing of 0.38 × 1e-9. Every baseline dimension then lands on the same line. DIMSPACE's default spacing has the same DIMSCALE 0 problem.

In AutoCAD the baseline offset is DIMDLI × the overall dimension scale of the dimension being continued, overrides included.

## Steps to reproduce

```
SETVAR DIMSCALE 10
DIMLINEAR 0,0 10,0 5,5
DIMBASELINE 20,0
```

(or `SETVAR DIMDLI 1` instead of `DIMSCALE 10`, or `-DIMSTYLE`/JSON `dimstyle {"name":"Standard","DIMSCALE":0}` then the same dimensions)

## Expected

- DIMSCALE 10: the second dimension line is at y = 5 + 0.38 × 10 = 8.8, clear of the 1.8-high text.
- DIMDLI 1: it is at y = 6.
- Style DIMSCALE 0 in model space: it is at y = 5.38 (scale 1, or the drawing's DIMSCALE).

## Actual

- DIMSCALE 10: y = 5.38, and the 1.8-high text of both dimensions overlaps.
- DIMDLI 1: y = 5.38.
- Style DIMSCALE 0: y = 5.00000000038, so both dimension lines coincide.

Cause: `chained()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/annotate.rs` computes `st.baseline_spacing * st.scale.max(1e-9)` from the bare style. It should use the style with the dimension's overrides, and `effective_scale` with the drawing's DIMSCALE, as rendering does. `run_dimspace` uses `st.scale.max(1e-9)` too.

title: fix(explode): exploded dimension text ignores DIM* overrides, DIMSCALE 0 and aligned text; DXF dimension blocks get the wrong text height
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

When a dimension is exploded, its text becomes an MTEXT whose height is the bare style's `DIMTXT × DIMSCALE` and whose rotation is always 0. The MTEXT does not match the text that was drawn:

- **Overrides are ignored.** A dimension made after `SETVAR DIMSCALE 10` (stored as an override since #129) draws 1.8-high text, but EXPLODE gives 0.18-high text. A `DIMTXT` override or DIMOVERRIDE is ignored in the same way. A text style with a fixed height is ignored too.
- **DIMSCALE 0 gives invisible text.** With a style DIMSCALE of 0 the dimension draws at scale 1, but the exploded text is 1.8e-10 high.
- **Aligned text turns horizontal.** With DIMTIH off (aligned text, as in ISO-style setups), a vertical dimension's text is drawn at 90°, but the exploded MTEXT is at 0°, lying across the dimension line.

DXF save has the same height bug. The anonymous `*D` block written for each dimension, which other programs draw, takes its MTEXT height from `style.text_height * style.scale.max(1e-9)`. Scaled or overridden dimensions therefore show wrong-sized text in other programs, and DIMSCALE 0 styles show no text there at all.

In AutoCAD, exploding a dimension leaves text that looks exactly like the dimension text did (same height, position and angle). The dimension block in a DXF file holds the dimension as drawn.

## Steps to reproduce

```
SETVAR DIMSCALE 10
DIMLINEAR 0,0 0,30 5,15
EXPLODE L
LIST L
```

Then, in a new drawing, `DIMTIH 0` (or JSON `dimstyle {"name":"Standard","DIMTIH":0}`), `DIMLINEAR 0,0 0,30 5,15`, `EXPLODE L`.

## Expected

- The MTEXT is 1.8 high, the height of the drawn dimension text.
- With DIMTIH 0 the MTEXT is rotated 90°, like the drawn text.
- A saved DXF's `*D` block MTEXT has the drawn height.

## Actual

- The MTEXT is 0.18 high (and 1.8e-10 with a style DIMSCALE of 0).
- The MTEXT rotation is 0.
- The `*D` block MTEXT height is the style's DIMTXT × DIMSCALE, without overrides or the DIMSCALE 0 fallback.

Cause: the Dimension arm of `exp…

title: fix(zoom): ZOOM inside a layout viewport fits and centres on the window, not the viewport, and nXP acts like nX
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Inside a layout viewport (after `MSPACE`), `ZOOM` works on the whole drawing window instead of the viewport:

- **Extents / All / Window / Object** fit the area to the window's aspect and paper-view height, not to the viewport. After `ZOOM E` most of the model lies outside the viewport and is clipped away.
- **In / Out / nX** zoom about the point under the middle of the window rather than the centre of the viewport, so the model drifts out of the viewport.
- **nXP** (`ZOOM 1/50XP`) is read as nX. AutoCAD uses nXP to set a viewport's scale relative to paper space, and `ZOOM 1/50XP` in a viewport is the usual way to set it to 1:50. Here it scales the current view instead, so the result depends on the zoom before it.

AutoCAD fits Extents/All/Window/Object to the active viewport, zooms In/Out/nX about the viewport centre, and gives the viewport a paper/model ratio of n for nXP. A locked viewport is left alone: the sheet zooms instead, and CADCraft already does that.

## Steps to reproduce

The drawing window is 1600×900 px (`viewport_px`), and the drawing is metric.

```
LINE 0,0 1000,0
LINE 0,0 0,500
LAYOUT  (layout.set Layout1)
MVIEW 20,20 120,100        (a 100 × 80 viewport)
MSPACE
ZOOM E
```

then, starting from a fresh viewport:

```
ZOOM 0.1XP
ZOOM 2X
ZOOM W 400,200 600,300
```

## Expected

- `ZOOM E`: the 1000 × 500 model extents fit in the 100 × 80 viewport, with view height ≥ 800 and view centre (500,250).
- `ZOOM 0.1XP`: the viewport scale becomes 0.1 (1:10), whatever it was before.
- `ZOOM 2X`: the view height halves and the view centre stays at (500,250).
- `ZOOM W 400,200 600,300`: the window fills the viewport, with view height 160 (200 wide at aspect 1.25) and centre (500,250).

## Actual

On upstream/main 9b7d7bd:

- `ZOOM E`: view height 190.3 and centre (334.2,135.9). Only a corner of the model shows, and on paper the content covers x 98–120, y 71–100 of the 20–120 × 20–100 viewport.
- `ZOOM 0.1XP`: scale 0.098 → 0.0098 (×0.1 of whatever …

title: fix(layout): undoing LAYOUT Rename/New on the current layout leaves the session on a layout that no longer exists
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Undo and redo restore the drawing but not the tab the session is showing. If you undo `LAYOUT Rename` or `LAYOUT New` while that layout is current, the session stays on a layout name that no longer exists. Nothing is drawn: no sheet and no viewports. Every command that adds geometry then fails with `no such space Paper("…")` until you click another tab.

In AutoCAD, undoing a rename keeps you on the same tab under its old name. Undoing the creation of the current layout returns you to an existing tab.

## Steps to reproduce

Undo of a rename:

```
LAYOUT          (layout.set Layout1)
layout.rename {"to": "Sheet"}
U
MVIEW 1,1 5,5
```

Undo of a new layout:

```
layout.new {"name": "New"}
layout.set {"name": "New"}
LINE 1,1 5,5
U
U
LINE 1,1 5,5
```

## Expected

- After the first `U`, the session shows `Layout1` with its sheet and viewports, and `MVIEW` adds a viewport there.
- After undoing `layout.new`, the session is on a layout that exists (or Model), and `LINE` works.

## Actual

On upstream/main 9b7d7bd:

- `layout_space()` is still `Paper("Sheet")`. The display list has no sheet, and `MVIEW` fails with `no such space Paper("Sheet")`.
- `layout_space()` is `Paper("New")`. `LINE` fails with `no such space Paper("New")`.

Redo has the same problem the other way round. For example, redoing a rename while the old-name tab is current.

title: fix(dim): DIMRND rounds tolerances and alternate units; DIMPOST added to angular dimensions
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Two problems with how dimension text is formatted (`linear_text` and the angular branch in `crates/render/src/dim.rs`):

**1. DIMRND rounds tolerances and alternate units.** The tolerance and alternate-unit number formats are copied from the primary format, so they inherit its DIMRND rounding increment (and its DIMZIN zero suppression).

- With DIMRND 0.5 and a ±0.1 tolerance, the tolerance is rounded to the nearest 0.5 and shows as `±0.0000`.
- With DIMALT on, the alternate value is rounded to the *primary* increment: 10.3 in with DIMRND 0.5 shows `[261.50]` (261.62 rounded to the primary 0.5 increment) instead of `[261.62]`.

In AutoCAD, DIMRND applies to the measurement only. Alternate units have their own variables: DIMALTRND (rounding), DIMALTU (unit format) and DIMALTZ (zero suppression). Tolerances have DIMTZIN (zero suppression). CADCraft has none of these, so they can't be set and are lost when a DXF is read.

**2. DIMPOST is added to angular dimensions.** With DIMPOST `<>mm`, an angular dimension reads `90°mm`. In the Dimension Style Manager, Prefix and Suffix (DIMPOST) are settings for linear dimensions only. Angular dimensions have their own unit format, precision and zero suppression, and no prefix or suffix.

## Steps to reproduce

```
SETVAR DIMRND 0.5
SETVAR DIMTOL 1
SETVAR DIMTP 0.1
SETVAR DIMTM 0.1
SETVAR DIMDEC 2
DIMLINEAR 0,0 10.3,0 0,5
```

Then, in a new drawing:

```
SETVAR DIMRND 0.5
SETVAR DIMALT 1
DIMLINEAR 0,0 10.3,0 0,5
```

Then, in a new drawing (Enter at the first DIMANGULAR prompt, then vertex, two angle endpoints and the arc location):

```
SETVAR DIMPOST <>mm
DIMANGULAR

0,0
10,0
0,10
3,3
```

Finally `SETVAR DIMALTRND 0.5`.

## Expected

- `10.50±0.1000` (DIMTDEC 4; the tolerance is not rounded).
- `10.5000 [261.62]` (the alternate value, 261.62, is rounded by DIMALTRND, which is 0 by default).
- The angular dimension reads `90°`.
- DIMALTRND, DIMALTU, DIMALTZ and DIMTZIN can be set (SETVAR, DIMSTYLE, overrides) and sur…

title: fix(dim): angular extension lines and DIMSE1/2 swap legs; centre mark drawn when the dimension line is inside the circle
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Two geometry problems in `dimension_geometry` (`crates/render/src/dim.rs`):

**1. Angular dimensions: extension lines go to the wrong leg when the arc is on the other side.** When the arc location lies outside the sweep from the first leg to the second, the arc is built from the second leg to the first (start and end swap). The extension lines, DIMSE1/DIMSE2 and DIMBLK1/DIMBLK2 still treat the arc start as leg 1. Each leg's extension line is then sized from the other leg's endpoint:

- A leg that ends short of the arc gets no extension line.
- A leg that already reaches past the arc gets one drawn along it.
- DIMSE1 suppresses the second leg's extension line, and DIMSE2 the first's.

**2. Radius and diameter dimensions always draw the DIMCEN centre mark.** It is drawn even when the dimension line is inside the circle: a diameter line through the centre, or a radius whose text is moved inside. The AutoCAD documentation of DIMCEN and of the Dimension Style Manager's Symbols and Arrows tab says that for DIMDIAMETER and DIMRADIUS the centre mark is drawn only when the dimension line is placed outside the circle or arc.

## Steps to reproduce

Angular (3-point form: Enter at the first prompt, then vertex, the two angle endpoints and the arc location):

```
DIMANGULAR

0,0
10,0
0,2
-3,-3
```

Then the same with `SETVAR DIMSE1 1` first.

Centre marks:

```
CIRCLE 0,0 5
DIMDIAMETER 5,0 8,0
DIMRADIUS 5,0 8,0
```

Then move the radius dimension's text inside the circle. Drag its text grip to 2,0, or use the JSON form `dimtedit {"handles":["<radius dim handle>"],"at":[2,0]}`, since DIMTEDIT has no typed form yet.

## Expected

- The 270° dimension has one extension line, along the second leg (0,0)-(0,2): it runs from just past (0,2) out to the arc at radius 4.24. The first leg (0,0)-(10,0) already crosses the arc, so it needs no extension line.
- With DIMSE1 on, the same output (the first leg had no extension line anyway). With DIMSE2 on, no extension lines.
- The …

title: fix(layout): typed LAYOUT / -LAYOUT has no option prompts, so its options run as commands
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Typing `LAYOUT` (or `-LAYOUT`) at the command line has no prompts. It runs the JSON default (a list) and ends at once, so the option and the layout names typed after it run as commands of their own. In a script, `LAYOUT N Sheet9` reports `unknown command n` and `unknown command Sheet9`, and no layout is created.

In AutoCAD, `-LAYOUT` asks `Enter layout option [Copy/Delete/New/Template/Rename/SAveas/Set/?] <set>:` and then asks for the layout name(s) the option needs. Scripts use it to create, copy, rename, delete and switch layouts. The `layout.*` engine commands can already do all of this. Only the prompts are missing.

## Steps to reproduce

```
LAYOUT
N
Sheet9
```

(or `LAYOUT N Sheet9` on one line, or `-LAYOUT S Layout2`)

## Expected

- `LAYOUT` prompts `Enter layout option [Copy/Delete/New/Template/Rename/SAveas/Set/?] <set>:`.
- `N`: `Enter name of new layout <Layout3>:`, and `Sheet9` creates the layout.
- Copy, Delete, Rename and Set ask for the layout(s) they act on. The current layout is the default.
- `?` lists the layouts.
- Template and SAveas say they are not available yet instead of doing something else.

## Actual

On upstream/main 1ff426d:

```
Command: LAYOUT
!! unknown command `n`
!! unknown command `Sheet9`
```

The layouts are still `Layout1, Layout2`. `-LAYOUT S Layout2` stays in the Model tab.

title: feat(snap): object snap tracking, Extension, Parallel and Apparent Intersection snaps (gaps.md U1)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Object snap tracking doesn't exist yet, and the Extension, Parallel and Apparent Intersection object snaps don't behave like AutoCAD's (docs/gaps.md U1, an alpha blocker). The OTRACK toggle (F11) does nothing.

## Expected

- **Object snap tracking (OTRACK, F11):** hovering over an object snap point acquires it (small `+` marker; hovering again releases it). Moving away shows alignment paths through acquired points — horizontal/vertical, or polar angles when POLARMODE says so — and the cursor snaps onto them. Intersections of two paths snap, and so do paths combined with a running object snap. Direct distance entry along a path works.
- **Extension (EXT):** hovering over the end of a line or arc shows its extension path; points on it snap.
- **Parallel (PAR):** after hovering over a line, a path parallel to it appears from the base point.
- **Apparent intersection (APP):** intersections of objects that don't actually meet, including their extensions.
- Tracking and the snaps must be scriptable and testable without the UI.

## Actual

There are no acquired points or alignment paths. EXT, PAR and APP have no real behaviour.

title: fix(layout): typed VPLAYER has no prompts, so its options run as commands (F starts FILLET)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Typing `VPLAYER` at the command line has no prompts. The command runs its JSON form with no parameters and ends, and whatever is typed next runs as a new command. In a script, `VPLAYER F 0` starts FILLET (`f`) and then fails on `0`, and no layer is frozen in the viewport.

In AutoCAD, `VPLAYER` asks `Enter an option [?/Color/Freeze/Thaw/Reset/Newfrz/Vpvisdflt]:`. It then asks for layer name(s) (wildcards allowed) and which viewports to apply the change to (`All/Select/Current/Except current`), and repeats until Enter. This is the usual way to freeze layers per viewport from a script. The engine can already apply per-viewport freezes and colours (`vplayer` / `viewport.set` JSON). Only the prompts are missing.

## Steps to reproduce

```
LINE 0,0 100,0
LAYOUT S Layout1       (or layout.set Layout1)
MVIEW 20,20 120,100
MSPACE
VPLAYER
F
0
          (Enter: Current viewport)
          (Enter: end)
```

## Expected

- `VPLAYER` prompts `Enter an option [?/Color/Freeze/Thaw/Reset/Newfrz/Vpvisdflt]:`.
- `F` asks for layer names. `0` asks `Enter an option [All/Select/Current/Except current] <Current>:`, and Enter freezes layer 0 in the current viewport.
- Thaw, Color, Reset, Newfrz, Vpvisdflt and `?` work the same way.

## Actual

On upstream/main 1ff426d:

```
Command: VPLAYER
Command: FILLET
Current settings: Mode = TRIM, Radius = 0.0000
```

The viewport's frozen-layer list stays `[]`.

title: fix(dim): DIMTEDIT has no command-line prompts (fails with "select dimensions" in scripts)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
DIMTEDIT has no command-line form. Typed at the command line or run from a script, it executes the JSON form at once with no selection and fails with "select dimensions", so a script cannot move, justify, rotate or home dimension text.

## Steps to reproduce
Script (or type at the command line):
```
DIMLINEAR 0,0 10,0 5,3
DIMTEDIT
```

## Expected
As in AutoCAD: `Select dimension:` (pick one dimension), then `Specify new location for dimension text or [Left/Right/Center/Home/Angle]:` — a point moves the text there; Left/Right/Center justify it along the dimension line; Home restores the default position; Angle asks `Specify angle for dimension text:` and rotates it.

## Actual
`dimtedit: select dimensions` error; no prompts. Only the menu entries (Dimension ▸ Align Text) and the JSON form with `handles` work.

title: fix(dim): DIMRADIUS/DIMDIAMETER ignore a dimension line location inside the circle (text always outside)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
DIMRADIUS (and DIMDIAMETER) ignore a dimension line location picked inside the circle: only the direction of the point is used, and the text is always placed outside the circle beyond the arrow.

## Steps to reproduce
```
CIRCLE 0,0 10
DIMRADIUS
```
pick the circle, then type `3,0` at `Specify dimension line location or [Mtext/Text/Angle]:` (a point inside the circle). Same with the JSON form: `dimradius {"handle": "<circle>", "at": [3, 0]}`.

## Expected
As in AutoCAD: a location inside the circle places the text inside, at that point on the radius, with the dimension line running from the text to the arrowhead on the circle (for a diameter, the dimension line spans the circle with the text on it). A location outside keeps the outside placement.

## Actual
The text is drawn outside the circle at about x = 13 (beyond the arrow at 10,0), with a leader line outward, wherever the point was picked.

title: fix(zoom): ZOOM Center/Scale/Dynamic do Zoom Extents, plain n acts like nX, and All/Extents in paper space fit the model limits
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Several typed `ZOOM` options do something other than what they say:

- **Center**, **Scale** and **Dynamic** all do Zoom Extents. None of them prompts for anything, so the centre point or factor typed after them runs as a new command, or fails.
- A plain number (`ZOOM 2`) acts like `2X`, relative to the current view. In AutoCAD, a number without X is a scale relative to the drawing limits, so `ZOOM 1` shows the limits at full size whatever the zoom was before.
- In paper space (a layout tab, not inside a viewport), **All** fits the **model** limits (LIMMIN/LIMMAX). **Extents** on an empty layout also falls back to the model limits. In paper space these should fit the sheet: the paper limits, together with the paper-space extents for All.

## Steps to reproduce

Metric drawing (limits 0,0–420,297), window 1600×900 px:

```
LINE 0,0 1000,0
ZOOM C 500,0 100
ZOOM S 2X
ZOOM 1
```

and in a layout with no viewports (`layout.set Layout1`, Letter sheet 279.4 × 215.9 mm):

```
ZOOM A
ZOOM E
```

## Expected

- `ZOOM C`: `Specify center point:` and then `Enter magnification or height <current>:`. `500,0 100` gives view centre (500,0) and height 100. `nX` and `nXP` are accepted as magnifications.
- `ZOOM S`: `Enter a scale factor (nX or nXP):`. `2X` halves the view height.
- `ZOOM 1`: the limits fill the view (height 297 at most aspect ratios), keeping the view centre.
- `ZOOM D`: cannot be dynamic without a mouse drag, so it should act like Window, not like Extents.
- Paper space `ZOOM A` and `ZOOM E`: the view fits the 279.4 × 215.9 sheet.

## Actual

On upstream/main 1ff426d:

- `ZOOM C`, `ZOOM S` and `ZOOM D` zoom to the extents at once. The following `500,0` / `2X` tokens then fail as commands.
- `ZOOM 1` leaves the view unchanged (×1 of the current view).
- Paper space `ZOOM A`: centre (210,148.5), height 313.8, which is the model limits 420 × 297. `ZOOM E`: centre (210,148.5), height 311.85. The sheet is 279.4 × 215.9.

title: fix(dim): DIMPOST suffix is not applied to tolerance values
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
With tolerances on (DIMTOL 1), the DIMPOST suffix is added to the main measurement only. AutoCAD's DIMPOST also applies the suffix to the tolerance values.

## Steps to reproduce
```
DIMPOST mm
DIMTOL 1
DIMTP 0.1
DIMTM 0.2
DIMLINEAR 0,0 10,0 5,3
```
(and with DIMTP = DIMTM for a symmetric ±0.1 tolerance.)

## Expected
`10.0000mm` followed by the stacked deviations `+0.1000mm` / `-0.2000mm` (symmetric: `10.0000mm±0.1000mm`).

## Actual
`10.0000mm` with the deviations `+0.1000` / `-0.2000` (symmetric: `10.0000mm±0.1000`): the tolerance values have no suffix.

Area: `linear_text` in `crates/render/src/dim.rs`.

title: feat(input): FROM, M2P/MTP, point filters, * prefix and <angle override at point prompts (gaps.md U3)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

The precision-input modifiers that AutoCAD users type at point prompts are missing (docs/gaps.md U3, an alpha blocker): `FROM`, `M2P`/`MTP`, point filters `.x`/`.y`/`.z`/`.xy`/`.xz`/`.yz`, the `*` absolute/WCS prefix, and the angle override `<a`. Temporary tracking (`TK`) is left to the object snap tracking work in #379.

## Expected

- **`FROM`:** asks for a base point, then `<Offset>:`, and accepts `@dx,dy` or `@d<a` relative to that base.
- **`M2P` / `MTP`:** asks for the first and second point and returns the midpoint between them.
- **Point filters:** `.x`, `.y`, `.xy` and the others take the named coordinates from one point and ask for the rest ("(need YZ)").
- **`*x,y` / `*@…`:** coordinates are taken in WCS. There is no UCS yet, so this matches the plain form, but it must parse.
- **`<a` at a point prompt:** locks the direction for the next point, and a typed distance then follows that angle.
- All of these work at any point prompt, in scripts and from the command line, and can be nested with object snaps (e.g. `FROM` then `END`).

## Actual

Each of these is reported as an unknown input or an invalid point.

title: feat(input): typed object snap overrides, Shift+right-click snap menu, Tab cycling (gaps.md U4)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Typed object snap overrides at a point prompt aren't supported (docs/gaps.md U4, an alpha blocker): `END`, `MID`, `CEN`, `GCE`, `NOD`, `QUA`, `INT`, `APP`, `EXT`, `INS`, `PER`, `TAN`, `NEA`, `PAR` and `NON` (also with their long names and the `_`/`'` prefixes). There is also no Shift/Ctrl+right-click snap menu and no Tab snap cycling.

## Expected

- Typing a snap mode at a point prompt applies that snap to the next pick only, overriding the running object snaps. In scripts, the next typed point is snapped with that mode when it lands within the aperture of an object.
- `NON` turns snapping off for the next pick.
- Shift+right-click (and Ctrl+right-click) on the canvas opens the object snap menu (Temporary track point, From, Mid Between 2 Points, the snap modes, None, Osnap Settings…), and choosing an entry applies that one-shot override.
- Tab cycles through the candidate snaps under the cursor.

## Actual

Typed snap names are unknown input, and there is no snap menu.

title: fix(layout): a viewport on a frozen layer still shows its contents
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Freezing the layer a layout viewport is on hides only the viewport's border: the model-space contents seen through the viewport keep showing, on screen and when plotting/exporting the layout. In AutoCAD, freezing the viewport's layer hides the viewport's contents too (turning the layer off hides only the border).

## Steps to reproduce
```
CIRCLE 0,0 5
LAYOUT Set Layout1
-LAYER Make VPORTS
MVIEW 1,1 9,7
-LAYER Freeze VPORTS
```
(the drawing must have another current layer for the freeze, e.g. `-LAYER Set 0` before freezing), then look at the layout or plot/export it (PDF/SVG/PNG).

## Expected
Neither the viewport border nor the circle seen through it is shown or plotted while VPORTS is frozen. With VPORTS only turned off, the circle shows and the border does not.

## Actual
The border disappears but the circle is still drawn inside the viewport, on screen and in plots.

Area: `viewport()` in `crates/render/src/lib.rs` (shared by `build` and `build_plot`).

title: feat(modify/draw): implement the remaining stubbed options in TRIM/EXTEND, PLINE arc mode and XLINE (gaps.md F1)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Several of the most-used commands still answer "not available yet" for options their prompts list (docs/gaps.md F1, an alpha blocker; Top-10 #5). Remaining on main:

- **TRIM / EXTEND**: cuTting edges, Fence, Crossing, mOde (Quick/Standard), Project, Edge (extend/no extend), eRase, Undo
- **PLINE arc mode**: Angle, CEnter, Direction, Radius, Second pt (and Line/Close/Halfwidth/Width from arc mode)
- **XLINE**: any of Hor/Ver/Ang/Bisect/Offset that are still stubbed (Ang Reference, Offset Through)

## Expected

Each option behaves as in AutoCAD and is usable from scripts and the command line. JSON forms gain equivalent parameters where it makes sense. Options that can't be supported say so without taking the next input.

## Actual

Each prints "<option>: not available yet".

title: feat(agents): guide desktop users through CLI and MCP setup
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Help a person connect an agent to CADCraft from the desktop app, with a checked CLI invocation and usable MCP configuration.

## Problem to solve

A desktop installation does not tell the user whether an agent can find the CLI, initialize MCP, or reach the open drawing. macOS distributes the CLI separately. Windows and Linux package it in different locations, sometimes inside a portable or container package. Copying a bare executable name leaves those differences unresolved.

## Proposed behavior

Add a discoverable desktop entry for agent setup. Distinguish the external automation CLI from the drawing command line inside the window.

Locate CLI candidates, show the selected command and version, and allow another installation. If none works, offer a matching official platform and release download or installation route. Check the resulting command before using it. Support today's separate CLI downloads independently of improvements to desktop packaging.

Explain headless MCP as a separate session and connected MCP as access to the running app. Produce client-ready configuration or a registration command with the actual executable path or wrapper arguments. Identify the connected target and explain launch or authorization prerequisites.

Offer a local check that starts the selected command, initializes MCP, and discovers tools without editing the drawing. Show client registration separately through instructions or an explicit action. A successful local check cannot establish registration in an external client.

## Acceptance criteria

- For live-app setup, a bounded non-mutating request must reach the intended running app and identify the relevant document, project, session or library. Report an unavailable or wrong target, and any headless fallback, separately from local stdio readiness; initialization and tool discovery alone do not verify live-app access.
- A desktop user can discover setup, inspect the exact command and version, and recover from a miss…

title: feat(distribution): provide reliable CLI access with desktop packages
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Give desktop installations of CADCraft a documented CLI invocation that people, scripts, and agents can use on Windows, Linux, and macOS.

## Problem to solve

Including a CLI executable in a package does not always make a shell command available. Windows installs the CLI beside the app; Linux native packages install it in `/usr/bin`, while AppImage and Flatpak keep it inside their package. macOS publishes a separate CLI download. Users need a supported invocation that matches their desktop installation without guessing its location or modifying global settings.

## Proposed behavior

Provide a callable CLI with each desktop distribution or an integrated installation route where needed, and document the exact invocation outside the agent setup UI. Preserve the existing CLI commands and MCP subcommand.

For Windows MSI, document full-path invocation of the installed CLI and make any shell exposure an explicit choice. Portable ZIP users can run its included executable without a global installation. For Linux DEB/RPM, preserve the existing `/usr/bin` CLI. Provide supported AppImage and Flatpak invocation through a wrapper or command override with the required arguments. For macOS, supply a compatible CLI with the desktop distribution or through its integrated installation route so users need not manually coordinate another download.

Define update, relocation, and removal behavior for each advertised invocation. Managed launchers must not become stale or overwrite a separately installed CLI. Keep the standalone CLI download supported for users who do not want the GUI.

## Acceptance criteria

- Linux tarball users can invoke the extracted CLI using the advertised path or optional installation procedure without building from source.
- A fresh Windows MSI installation has a documented full-path command that reports its matching CLI version. A fresh portable ZIP works from its extracted directory, including paths with spaces.
- Fresh Linux DEB/RPM installation…
