title: feat(file): autosave (SAVETIME), crash recovery, AUDIT and RECOVER (gaps.md F4)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

There is no autosave, no crash recovery file, and no AUDIT or RECOVER (docs/gaps.md F4, Top-10 #8). If the app or the machine goes down, unsaved work is lost, and damaged drawings can't be repaired.

## Expected

- **Autosave (SAVETIME minutes, default 10; 0 = off):** each drawing with unsaved changes is written in the background to an autosave file (`<name>_<id>.sv$`-style, as a DXF/DWG CADCraft can read) in a per-user autosave folder (SAVEFILEPATH). The file is deleted on a normal save or close.
- **Crash recovery:** on the next start, autosave files left over from a crash are offered for recovery (Drawing Recovery list: open the recovered copy, or discard it).
- **AUDIT [Yes/No]:** checks the drawing for errors (dangling handles and references, missing layers/linetypes/styles/blocks, invalid geometry such as NaN or zero-length, block cycles, duplicate handles), reports what it found and fixes it when told Yes. Programmatic form returns the report.
- **RECOVER file:** opens a damaged DXF/DWG as tolerantly as possible, runs AUDIT's fixes and reports them.
- Native on desktop. The web build keeps autosave in browser storage, or says it isn't available.

## Actual

None of these exist: there is no SAVETIME anywhere.

title: feat(draw/annotate): remaining stubbed options in SPLINE, MTEXT and MLEADER (gaps.md F1)
author: vangel76
body:

These options still answer "not available yet" (docs/gaps.md F1 after #397, part of the alpha gate):

- **SPLINE:** Knots (Chord/Square root/Uniform), Object (convert a spline-fit polyline), start and end Tangency, toLerance
- **MTEXT** (command-line options before the text): Height, Justify, Line spacing, Rotation, Style, Width, Columns
- **MLEADER:** the options #247 left as "not available yet": spline leaders, no-leader content, and block content

## Expected

Each option behaves as in AutoCAD and works from scripts and the command line, with JSON equivalents where sensible. Unsupported options say so without taking the next input.

## Actual

Each prints "<option>: not available yet".

title: feat(plot): apply plot style tables (CTB/STB) to plots and layouts (gaps.md F14)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary

Plot styles aren't applied (docs/gaps.md F14, an alpha blocker): a layout's or page setup's plot style table (CTB/STB) is stored but ignored when plotting or exporting, so sheets can't come out monochrome or with pen-assigned lineweights the way offices plot.

## Expected

- **Colour-dependent plot styles (CTB, PSTYLEMODE=1, the default):** the plot style table set in the page setup maps each ACI colour to an output colour (including "use object colour"), screening, linetype ("use object linetype"), lineweight ("use object lineweight"), end and join style, and fill style. CADCraft ships its own built-in tables, as original definitions: `monochrome.ctb` (everything black), `grayscale.ctb`, and none/`acad.ctb`-equivalent (object colours, our own name).
- **Named plot styles (STB, PSTYLEMODE=0):** a PlotStyle property on layers and objects (ByLayer/ByBlock/name), resolved against an STB table. Partial is fine: the property is stored and round-tripped, and the table is applied.
- **Where it applies:** PDF plots (PLOT, PUBLISH, the Plot dialog from #200), and "display plot styles" in layouts (the page setup flag) for the screen and the PNG/SVG exports of a layout.
- **Tables are files:** load/save in our own documented format, and read the binary CTB/STB format if feasible from public descriptions (CTB is zlib-compressed text). Never ship Autodesk's .ctb files.
- **PLOTSTYLE / STYLESMANAGER commands:** set an object's plot style, list the tables, and edit a table's entries (JSON form plus a basic dialog).

## Actual

The plot style table name round-trips through DXF (#209/#216), but nothing reads it.

title: Proposal: SolidCraft, a parametric 3D CAD craft on a shared B-rep kernel
author: lpgn
body:
Hi echelon and the ArtCraft team. After the WordCraft PRs (#124, #125, #178) I looked at the craft family, and one big app is missing: parametric 3D CAD, in the style of SOLIDWORKS. I would like to know if you want this under ArtCraft before anyone writes code.

## Why

- No craft does parametric 3D. CADCraft has the same gap: F24 in its `docs/gaps.md` says there is no 3D yet (300–450 h). Both apps need the same thing first: a B-rep kernel.
- One kernel crate in `craft-libs` (for example `craft-brep`) can serve CADCraft 3D solids and a SolidCraft. The hardest part is then done once.
- A clear gain over SOLIDWORKS: its rebuild, mates and sketch solver run on one core, so its hardware advice is "high clock speed, not more cores". Only simulation and rendering scale. A kernel and feature tree designed for many cores and the GPU from day 1 is a real difference, not only a copy.

## Same rules as the other crafts

- Clean room: observe SOLIDWORKS black-box only. Rust only, wasm stays green, MIT/Apache, no GPL/LGPL code (so no OpenCASCADE).
- Everything is a `CommandSpec`; parity is measured against the SOLIDWORKS menus with `cargo xtask parity`. Never crash: a failed feature is a rebuild error, never a panic.
- Formats only from public specs: STEP (ISO 10303), Parasolid XT (Siemens publishes the format reference), STL, 3MF, DXF. Native SLDPRT/SLDASM has no public spec, so it is out. Users exchange files through STEP or x_t.
- The agent channel from WordCraft (control key, chat, MCP, guard) carries over.

## Parallel and GPU by design

- The feature tree is a dependency graph, not a list: independent branches rebuild in parallel. Each part of an assembly rebuilds on its own core.
- Inside one operation, face-pair intersections, tessellation, mass properties and drawing views run with rayon.
- wgpu for display of large assemblies, NURBS tessellation in compute shaders, ID-buffer picking and hidden-line removal. Exact booleans stay on the CPU (f64, robust predicates).
- A c…

Feature control frames can be created, edited, rendered, saved and reopened.

title: feat(file): save DWG/DXF at a chosen version (2000–2018) and binary DXF (gaps.md FF3)

## Scope

- Binary DXF writing (and reading if missing).

title: feat(modify): associative arrays — ASsociative, Levels, polar rows, ARRAYEDIT (gaps.md F5)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Arrays are not associative (`docs/gaps.md` F5). ARRAY, ARRAYRECT and ARRAYPOLAR create plain copies. ASsociative, Levels, polar ROWs and grip editing print "not available yet", and there is no ARRAYEDIT.

## Scope
- Associative array object: source objects held in an anonymous block, plus parameters (rectangular: columns/rows/levels with spacing and the axis angle; polar: count/fill angle/rotate items/rows/levels). It regenerates when edited.
- ASsociative Yes/No in ARRAYRECT and ARRAYPOLAR (Yes by default, as in AutoCAD); Levels; polar ROWs.
- ARRAYEDIT: change the parameters, Source (edit the source objects), Replace items, Reset, and EXPLODE to plain objects.
- Grips on associative arrays (count and spacing) if they fit; otherwise parameter editing only.
- DXF/DWG: written so other programs see the items (an anonymous block plus an INSERT, with the parameters kept in our own data); round trip inside CADCraft keeps it associative. Clean-room: no copying of the undocumented ACAD_EVALUATION_GRAPH.
- ARRAYPATH can stay non-associative if it doesn't fit; list it under Limits.
- JSON forms; programmatic calls never open dialogs.

## Expected
Arrays can be edited after creation, like publicly documented AutoCAD associative arrays.

title: feat(hatch): associative hatches follow their boundary, hatch origin, gap tolerance, separate hatches (gaps.md F13)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Hatching lacks core editing behaviour (`docs/gaps.md` F13).
- Associative hatches don't follow when their boundary moves or changes.
- The hatch origin can't be set.
- There is no gap tolerance (HPGAPTOL).
- "Create separate hatches" is missing.
- HATCHEDIT can't recreate the boundary.

## Scope
- Associativity: a hatch keeps the handles of its boundary objects. MOVE, STRETCH, grip edits, SCALE and similar on a boundary object re-fill the hatch. Erasing a boundary object, or opening a gap in the boundary, drops associativity with a message. The link survives DXF save and reopen (group 97/330 source boundary objects, public DXF Reference).
- Origin: HATCH and HATCHEDIT Origin option (Use current origin / Set new origin / bottom-left of the extents…); HPORIGIN, HPORIGINMODE.
- Gap tolerance: HPGAPTOL, so pick-point region detection closes small gaps.
- HPSEPARATE / Separate: several picked areas give separate hatches.
- HATCHEDIT: Associativity on/off, Separate, Origin, Recreate boundary (-HATCHEDIT Boundary).
- JSON forms; programmatic calls never open dialogs.
- Correct the F13 row where earlier fixes already landed (#289 island style/background/gradients, #213 origin read/write).

## Expected
Hatches behave like publicly documented AutoCAD associative hatches.

title: feat(layout): polygonal, object and clipped viewports, MVIEW Lock/ON/OFF/Fit/2/3/4, VPCLIP, viewport scale (gaps.md F15)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Layout viewports are limited to rectangles (`docs/gaps.md` F15). Missing:
- polygonal, object and clipped viewports;
- MVIEW's Lock, ON/OFF, Fit, Restore and 2/3/4 options;
- VPCLIP;
- a viewport scale control in the UI.

## Scope
- MVIEW: Polygonal (pick vertices, with Arc segments where it fits), Object (convert a closed polyline, circle, ellipse, spline or region into a viewport boundary), Lock On/Off, ON/OFF, Fit, Restore (from named viewport configurations if VPORTS exist; otherwise "not available yet"), 2/3/4 viewports, with both the typed form and the JSON form.
- VPCLIP: clip an existing viewport with an object or a polygon, and Delete to remove the clip.
- Clipped viewports: render model space clipped to the boundary on screen and in PNG/SVG/PDF plots. A locked viewport refuses zoom and pan inside it.
- DXF: viewport clip boundary handle (group 340), status flags (90: locked, non-rectangular clipping, on/off), round trip per the public DXF Reference.
- UI: a viewport scale list on the status bar for the active viewport, kept thin.
- Programmatic calls never open dialogs.

## Expected
Viewports behave like publicly documented AutoCAD layout viewports.

title: feat(dxf): native MULTILEADER and MLEADERSTYLE read/write instead of LEADER+MTEXT (gaps.md FF2)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Multileaders aren't native objects (`docs/gaps.md` FF2). MLEADER is saved as LEADER + MTEXT/INSERT, and MULTILEADER entities in an opened DXF/DWG are kept as unknown data or broken apart. A drawing round-tripped through CADCraft loses its multileaders as such.

## Scope
- Read MULTILEADER entities (the public DXF Reference: the context data block with leader roots and lines, the content block or MText data, the arrowhead, the landing/dogleg and the MLEADERSTYLE handle) into the MLeader model. That covers straight and spline leaders, several leader lines, MText and block content with attribute values, and the text attachment.
- Write MULTILEADER (and MLEADERSTYLE objects in the ACAD_MLEADERSTYLE dictionary) instead of LEADER + MTEXT, at the versions we write (2000 and later). Keep an option or fallback only if the format needs one.
- DWG through the acadrust bridge, where it maps.
- Hostile input: clamp counts and nesting, skip bad handles, never panic.
- Round-trip tests: MLEADER → DXF → reopen gives the same entity, style and content.

## Expected
Multileaders survive save and reopen as multileaders, and other programs see real MULTILEADER entities.

title: feat(edit): UNDO Mark/Back/BEgin/End/Auto/Control, MREDO, wider SETVAR coverage (gaps.md U10)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
The UNDO command lists Auto, Control, BEgin, End, Mark and Back, but they don't work (`docs/gaps.md` U10). SETVAR also covers only about 60 system variables.

## Scope
- UNDO Mark and Back: Back undoes to the last mark, and asks for confirmation when there is no mark.
- UNDO BEgin and End: group the operations in between into one undo step. Scripts and the JSON form must be able to do this too.
- UNDO Auto and Control (All/None/One/Combine):
  - None turns undo off.
  - One allows a single step.
  - Combine merges consecutive zoom and pan steps.
- UNDOCTL, read-only: shows the current state.
- REDO and MREDO with a count.
- Widen SETVAR/GETVAR to the common drawing and session variables that the engine already models but doesn't expose, generated from the existing settings rather than handwritten one by one. Unknown variables still give a clear error.
- JSON forms for all of the above; programmatic calls never open dialogs.

## Expected
UNDO and SETVAR behave like the publicly documented AutoCAD commands.

title: feat(view): named views (VIEW), tiled model viewports (VPORTS), MVIEW Restore, Zoom Realtime/Dynamic, ZOOMFACTOR (gaps.md U11)
author: vangel76

## Summary
Several view tools are missing (`docs/gaps.md` U11):
- Zoom Realtime and Dynamic, and ZOOMFACTOR;
- named views (VIEW);
- tiled model-space viewports (VPORTS);
- named viewport configurations, so MVIEW Restore prints "not available yet" (#453).

## Scope
- VIEW / -VIEW: Save, Restore, Delete, list (?), Orthographic left out (2D only). Named views keep the centre, height/width, twist, layer snapshot (optional) and the space or layout. Stored in the drawing and round-tripped through the DXF VIEW table (public DXF Reference). Restore is a view change, as an undo step like ZOOM.
- VPORTS / -VPORTS in model space: Single, 2/3/4 (with arrangement), Join, Save/Restore/Delete named configurations; the active tile follows the click; each tile keeps its own view; DXF VPORT table (*ACTIVE entries plus named configurations).
- MVIEW Restore: insert a named viewport configuration into a layout.
- ZOOM Realtime (drag zoom, an interactive mode the UI drives) and Dynamic (view box over the extents), ZOOMFACTOR for the wheel.
- Keep the UI thin: tiles drawn by the canvas from engine state.

Views and tiled viewports behave like publicly documented AutoCAD.

title: feat(modify): TRIM/EXTEND/FILLET/CHAMFER/JOIN/LENGTHEN on ellipses and splines (gaps.md F6)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
The modify commands don't handle ellipses and splines (`docs/gaps.md` F6): FILLET, CHAMFER, JOIN, LENGTHEN, EXTEND and TRIM refuse or ignore elliptical arcs and splines. #248 fixed FILLET Trim/Multiple and CHAMFER Angle/mEthod, so that part of the row is out of date.

## Scope
- TRIM and EXTEND: elliptical arcs and open splines as objects to trim/extend, and as cutting/boundary edges (extending a spline along its end tangent; extending an elliptical arc along its ellipse).
- FILLET: line/arc/ellipse/spline combinations. The fillet arc is tangent to both curves; the curves are trimmed by trimming the elliptical arc parameter, or by splitting the spline at the tangent point.
- CHAMFER: lines with elliptical arcs or splines where AutoCAD supports it; otherwise a clear message.
- JOIN: elliptical arcs on the same ellipse (into a larger arc or a full ellipse); splines and lines/arcs/polylines joined end to end into a spline.
- LENGTHEN: elliptical arcs (DElta/Percent/Total/DYnamic along the ellipse); open splines (where AutoCAD supports it).
- FILLET and CHAMFER between polyline segments and other objects, if still missing.
- Numeric robustness: iterative solvers with capped iterations, never panic on degenerate input.

## Expected
These commands work on ellipses and splines like publicly documented AutoCAD.

title: fix(dimstyle): deletion removes a style used by a block dimension
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`dimstyle.delete` successfully removes a dimension style that a dimension inside an inserted block still uses. Saving the drawing keeps that dimension's old style reference while omitting the style from the DIMSTYLE table. The equivalent model-space dimension correctly prevents deletion. This leaves a dangling reference in an otherwise intact drawing.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the debug CLI from the current-source baseline under Runtime or environment in an empty disposable directory. These commands create the complete drawing through supported operations. `keep:"convert"` replaces the selected dimension with a live insert of its new block, so the definition is used by the drawing.

```sh
export CADCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR="$PWD/cadcraft-config"

cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'dimstyle {"name":"DS","DIMTXT":2}' \
  --cmd 'dimlinear {"p1":[0,0],"p2":[10,0],"at":[5,3]}' \
  --cmd 'selectall {}' \
  --cmd 'block {"name":"BD","base":[0,0],"keep":"convert"}' \
  --save block-before.dxf

cadcraft-cli run block-before.dxf \
  --cmd 'dimstyle.current {"name":"Standard"}' \
```

title: feat(dxf): read pre-2007 files in their $DWGCODEPAGE (CJK, Cyrillic, Central European…) (gaps.md FF4)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Pre-2007 DXF and DWG files are read as if every byte were Latin-1/UTF-8, whatever `$DWGCODEPAGE` they declare (`docs/gaps.md` FF4, Top-10 #4). Japanese (ANSI_932), Chinese (936/950), Korean (949) and Cyrillic, Central European, Greek and Turkish (ANSI_1250–1258) drawings open with garbled text, layer names and block names.

## Scope
- DXF reader: honour `$DWGCODEPAGE` for files before AC1021 (2007). Decode strings from that code page; keep the `\U+XXXX` and `\M+nXXXX` escapes working as today.
- Supported code pages: ANSI_874, 932, 936, 949, 950 and 1250–1258, plus the DOS code pages where they map cleanly. An unknown code page falls back to the current behaviour with a warning.
- Binary DXF: same handling.
- DWG through the acadrust bridge: check that pre-2007 DWG text decodes with the file's code page. Fix it in the bridge, or report the gap.
- Writer: pre-2007 output stays ASCII with `\U+` escapes (correct for any code page). Keep `$DWGCODEPAGE` as read, so a round trip preserves it.
- Decoding is a pure function in a low layer. Hostile input (invalid multibyte sequences, truncated lead bytes) never panics.
- Dependencies: a pure-Rust, wasm-friendly, permissively licensed decoder (e.g. encoding_rs) only if the ADR allows it. Otherwise use our own tables generated from public Unicode mapping data, with attribution.

## Expected
Old drawings in non-Latin code pages open with correct text.

title: feat(draw): MLINE entity with MLSTYLE/MLEDIT, REGION entity, HELIX entity (gaps.md F21)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
Three draw commands make stand-ins instead of real objects (`docs/gaps.md` F21):
- MLINE draws two polylines; there is no MLINE entity and no MLSTYLE.
- REGION makes polylines; there is no region entity.
- HELIX makes a polyline.
So these objects can't be edited as what they are, and other programs see the wrong entity types.

## Scope
- **MLINE entity and MLSTYLE:**
  - doc model: elements with offset, colour and linetype; caps and joints; fill;
  - MLINE command with Justification, Scale and STyle;
  - the MLSTYLE command with a JSON form, and MLEDIT basics (Close/Open/Merged cross, tee, corner joint, add/delete vertex, cut/weld) where they fit;
  - render, grips and snaps; EXPLODE gives lines/arcs;
  - DXF MLINE and MLINESTYLE (ACAD_MLINESTYLE dictionary) per the public DXF Reference.
- **REGION entity:**
  - a closed planar boundary of loops, with outer and island loops;
  - REGION from closed objects; UNION/SUBTRACT/INTERSECT on regions if 2D boolean geometry exists or is cheap, otherwise "not available yet";
  - area and perimeter in AREA/MASSPROP; EXPLODE gives the boundary curves.
  - DXF REGION is ACIS data (SAT), which isn't publicly specified to the needed depth: keep foreign REGIONs as unknown data as today; write ours as REGION only if a minimal SAT body can be built from public information, otherwise write the boundary as a closed polyline plus our own xdata, and list it under Limits.
- **HELIX:** a HELIX entity (base/top radius, turns, height, turn direction) drawn as a spline. DXF HELIX (subclass AcDbHelix on top of SPLINE) per the public DXF Reference.

## Expected
These objects are real entities that can be edited, saved and reopened.

title: feat(xref): external references — XATTACH, XREF palette, overlay, paths, reload/unload/detach, BIND/XBIND (gaps.md F2)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
External references are missing (`docs/gaps.md` F2, alpha blocker): XATTACH, the XREF palette, overlay, path handling, BIND, REFEDIT and XCLIP. #213 now keeps xref block paths through a DXF save, but the referenced drawings are never loaded or drawn.

## Scope (part 1 here; REFEDIT and XCLIP as follow-ups if they don't fit)
- **Xref model:** a block definition flagged as an xref (attach or overlay) with a path. The path is saved as given (full, relative or none) and resolved against the host drawing's folder, the saved path and a search path (PROJECTNAME/XREF search paths kept simple).
- **Loading:** a referenced DXF or DWG is read through the io read hook. Its model space becomes the block's content, and its layers, linetypes and styles are prefixed `xref|name`. Nesting is bounded (MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH); circular references are detected; missing files are reported as "Not Found" without breaking the host.
- **Commands:**
  - XATTACH (path, Attach/Overlay, insertion/scale/rotation);
  - XREF / -XREF (?/Bind/Detach/Path/Unload/Reload/Overlay/Attach);
  - XBIND (bind individual named objects);
  - BIND (Bind/Insert) turns an xref into a normal block.
  - JSON forms; programmatic calls never open dialogs (no file picker from JSON).
- **External References palette:** a list with status (Loaded/Unloaded/Not Found/Unreferenced), type and path, plus Reload/Detach/Unload/Bind/Open. Kept thin.
- **DXF:** xref BLOCK flags (4 xref, 8 overlay, 32 resolved) and the path (group 1). Xref-dependent table entries (flag 16/32 with `|` names) are not written as local tables. Round trip keeps the xref unresolved-but-intact.
- **Web build:** no file system, so xrefs stay unloaded with a clear status.
- **Never crash:** a hostile or huge referenced file is capped by the existing read limits; a failed load leaves an empty, flagged block.

## Expected
Multi-file projects open with their xrefs shown, and xrefs can be attached, reloaded, detached and bound.

title: feat(text): MTEXT columns, bullets/numbering, tabs and indents, FIELD/UPDATEFIELD, SPELL; in-place editor (gaps.md F9)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
MTEXT is limited (`docs/gaps.md` F9). It has:
- no columns;
- no bullets or numbering;
- no tabs or indents;
- no fields (FIELD, UPDATEFIELD);
- no spell check (SPELL).

Text is edited in a dialog box instead of in place. #408 left MTEXT Columns Dynamic/Static as "not available yet".

## Scope, part 1 (formatting and fields)
- MTEXT paragraph formatting from the MTEXT format codes in the public DXF Reference (`\p` paragraph: indents i/l/r, tabs t, bullets/numbering x… where documented; `\P`). Covered in the model, layout and rendering, with a lossless round trip of the codes.
- Columns: none, static and dynamic. Column width, gutter and height; text flows into the next column. Covered in the model, DXF (MTEXT column data, groups 75/76/78/79/48/49/50 per the DXF Reference), MTEXT Columns options and rendering.
- FIELD: insert a field (Date/SaveDate/Filename/Author/Title/object property such as Area/Length of a handle). The field is stored in MTEXT/TEXT as `%<\AcVar …>%`/`%<\AcObjProp …>%` where publicly documented, otherwise as our own expression format. UPDATEFIELD and FIELDEVAL/FIELDDISPLAY; the evaluated value is shown with the grey background.
- SPELL: check words in TEXT/MTEXT/attributes against a word list loaded from a user dictionary file (no bundled dictionary unless a permissively licensed one is attributed in ATTRIBUTION.md).

## Scope, part 2 (follow-up)
- In-place MTEXT editor on the canvas, replacing the dialog box: a text box at the MTEXT location, a ruler for indents and tabs, and a formatting toolbar.

## Expected
MTEXT supports the paragraph formatting, columns and fields that real drawings use.

title: `cadcraft-cli` panics (exit 101) when stdout is closed early
author: wzsxb233
body:
**Summary**

`cadcraft-cli commands | head` aborts with a Rust panic: `failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)`, exit status 101 under `pipefail`. The same command on designcraft, deckcraft, gridcraft and soundcraft exits quietly. FilmCraft fixed the same panic in #285.

**Environment**

- CADCraft v0.5.0 @ 315751e3ec98e708bcc831dd7f80ca0433a2e3d0, `cadcraft-cli` release build
- Linux x86_64, Rust 1.99.0

**Steps**

```sh
set -o pipefail
cadcraft-cli commands | head -c 20 >/dev/null
echo $?
```

**Expected**

Exit 0 (or a normal non-panic status) once the reader closes stdout. No panic message.

**Actual**

Exit 101. Stderr:

```text
thread 'main' panicked at library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1168:9:
failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)
```

`cadcraft-cli commands` is about 4,000 lines, so the write does not fit in the pipe buffer. A small `info` of a one-entity DXF piped to `head -c 20` exits 0, because that write finishes before the pipe closes.

title: Feature request: AutoSave, backups and drawing locks for DWG/DXF on storage you own (local/NAS, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3/R2 via rclone), with no silent overwrites
author: fernandodilland
body:
## TL;DR
Please add an open equivalent to AutoCAD's autosave/backup/lock files and to cloud-hosted drawings: a central "Save target" so a drawing can be backed up and versioned on storage the user owns, with a TTL lease instead of stale lock files, and sharing across drawings later. Opt-in, no vendor server, no telemetry. **Hard requirement: never overwrite the user's original DWG/DXF automatically.**

## Why
- The README says entities CADCraft doesn't model yet are not kept on save, and DWG/DXF are written as R2000. Overwriting the original in place from an autosave could silently drop geometry or downgrade the file.
- CAD users share drawings on network shares and cloud folders all the time, and a crash or a half-synced file is expensive.

## How AutoCAD does it
- Autosave is on by default, every 10 minutes (the SAVETIME variable), into `.sv$` files that are deleted on a clean exit. Saving also writes a `.bak` of the previous version. After a crash, the Drawing Recovery Manager offers the drawing, the `.bak`, the `.sv$` or a `_RECOVER` file.
- A save writes to a temp file first and then replaces the drawing.
- `.dwl`/`.dwl2` files are created next to the DWG while it is open. The documentation I found says they exist for the WHOHAS command (who has this drawing open), not as a hard lock, and that they linger after crashes and are overwritten when the drawing is reopened.
- Teams usually split a project into several DWGs linked as external references (xrefs), so ownership is per drawing.

## What CADCraft has today (README only)
DXF read R12-2018 and write R2000, DWG read R13-2018 and write R2000, command line and `.scr`-style scripts, associative dimensions, constraints that re-solve after each edit, CLI/MCP/control channel, web build.

## Proposal
**Phase 0, autosave + recovery:** write-ahead journal of commands/edits plus periodic snapshots in the native in-memory form; atomic writes; Drawing Recovery-style prompt on restart; `AUTOSAVE`/SAVETIME-like variable fo…

title: Window decorations and title bar inconsistent with VectorCraft / PhotoCraft
author: dylanmtaylor

### Description
The window decorations and title bar handling in `cadcraft` are inconsistent with the standard established in VectorCraft (PR #969) and PhotoCraft (PR #1903).

### Current Behavior
- On Windows and Linux, the application either does not draw client-side decorations/caption buttons or lacks consistent custom title bar handling.

2. Provide a `System Title Bar` preference under User Interface to allow users to switch back to native OS decorations on Windows/Linux if desired.
3. macOS retains native window buttons and fullsize content view.

title: fix(macos): shipped DMG app fails strict signature verification with FinderInfo metadata
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The official CADCraft macOS DMG contains an app that fails `codesign --verify --deep --strict`, both inside the mounted image and after copying it with `ditto`. Removing only `com.apple.FinderInfo` from the disposable copied app restores strict verification, and Gatekeeper then accepts it as `Notarized Developer ID`. This affects package verification; I did not test or establish a GUI launch failure.

## Runtime or environment

- Tested release: [v0.5.0](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/releases/tag/v0.5.0), the latest published release at this check.

- SHA-256: `f7c9a84707eae58405d8930764abfddacb89531571d63a4a49d9b9b735f6f8a7`. The fresh download matched both the release asset digest and the published `SHA256SUMS.txt` entry.
- Host: macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434, Apple silicon, `arm64`.
- Source inspection: current default branch `main`. Its macOS packaging script is byte-identical to the script at the tested release tag. This was an isolated test of the published binary, not a source rebuild.

## Steps to reproduce

Download the official artifact into a disposable directory and mount it read-only. These steps were executed on the measured host with a fresh download:

```sh
work=$(mktemp -d /tmp/craft-dmg.XXXXXX)

```

Confirm that the checksum matches the value above, then mount and check the app:

```sh
mkdir "$work/mount"
hdiutil attach -readonly -nobrowse -mountpoint "$work/mount" "$work/release.dmg"
codesign --verify --deep --strict "$work/mount/CADCraft.app"
xattr -l "$work/mount/CADCraft.app"
ditto "$work/mount/CADCraft.app" "$work/CADCraft.app"
codesign --verify --deep --strict "$work/CADCraft.app"
xattr -l "$work/CADCraft.app"
```

The two `codesign` commands are expected to fail in this reproduction; continue to record both result…

title: Canvas freezes on real DWG files: pattern hatches expand to ~30M primitives per zoom step (measurements + patch)
author: EP995LAB
body:
## Summary

Opening real-world DWG files (architectural plans, 7k–16k entities) makes the canvas freeze on zoom and pan: every 2x zoom step blocks for 1.1–1.6 s and the crosshair lags behind the mouse. Entity count is not the problem (your 200k-entity benchmark holds). **Pattern hatches are**: they are expanded dash by dash at full resolution, over the whole drawing, independently of the view. One plan with 483 hatches becomes **29.9 million primitives**, rebuilt at every zoom band.

Below are the measurements, the cause and a patch that fixes it (built and measured on 0.4.0; it conflicts with the hatch changes in 0.5.0, so it needs porting — happy for you to take it, rework it or ignore it).

## Measurements (0.4.0, release build, Apple silicon)

A new `cadcraft-cli perf FILE` mode (in the patch) builds the display list as the canvas does (1000 px tall view, the canvas' tolerance and dash bands) at zoom extents and 4x…1024x:

| Drawing | Entities | Primitives (before) | Build per zoom band (before) | Primitives (after) | Build (after) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Architectural plan A | 6,946 (483 hatches) | 29.9 M (29.2 M hatch dots) | 1,170–1,340 ms | 16–19 k | 6–13 ms |
| Architectural plan B | 11,837 (467 hatches) | 30.0 M | 1,400–1,620 ms | 41–49 k | 23–66 ms |
| Plant room plan | 16,152 (536 hatches) | 17.9 M (16.8 M hatch segments) | 1,110–1,270 ms | 92–168 k | 44–99 ms |

The per-type breakdown in the same tool shows hatches as >99 % of primitives. Pick and osnap were already fast (0.001–0.2 ms), so the "crazy cursor" is just the main thread blocked in `render::build` plus the GPU mesh rebuild.

## Cause

- `hatch::pattern_lines(h, tol)` ignores the pixel size: dashes and dots far below a pixel are emitted one by one.
- It ignores the view: every hatch is generated over its whole area even when zoomed into one room.
- `ensure_list` rebuilds the whole list at every 2x zoom band, so the cost is paid on every zoom step.
- Second cost: filled TrueType glyphs ar…

title: feat(constraints): DOF report, G2 Smooth, ellipse/spline/block geometry, CONSTRAINTINFER while drawing (gaps.md F25)
author: vangel76
body:
## Summary
The parametric constraint solver has gaps (`docs/gaps.md` F25; #73 was fixed by #190):
- There is no degrees-of-freedom (DOF) report and no "fully constrained" status.
- Smooth is G1, not G2 (curvature continuity).
- Ellipses, elliptical arcs, splines and block references can't take part in constraints.
- Nothing is inferred while drawing (CONSTRAINTINFER).

## Scope
- **DOF analysis:**
  - the remaining DOF per object and for the whole drawing;
  - under-, fully and over-constrained status;
  - the constraint bar and status show it; a JSON query returns it;
  - over-constrained additions are refused with a clear message, as today, plus the redundant-constraint hint.
- **Geometry:**
  - **Ellipses and elliptical arcs:** centre, axis endpoints and arc ends as constraint points; Tangent, Coincident, Concentric and Horizontal/Vertical on the major axis.
  - **Splines:** fit and control points as constraint points; Tangent and Smooth at ends.
  - **Block references:** the insertion point, and the block's geometry as rigid points for coincident/fixed constraints.
- **Smooth (G2):** curvature continuity between a spline and a line, arc or spline.
- **Inference:** CONSTRAINTINFER 1 adds Coincident, Horizontal/Vertical, Parallel/Perpendicular and Tangent while drawing and editing with snaps, as already done for autoTypes.
- **Solver robustness:** capped iterations, no NaN; hostile parameters never panic.
- Clean-room: our own solver code. Never read FreeCAD planegcs, SolveSpace or other GPL solvers.

## Expected
Constraints report their DOF and work on all common 2D geometry.

title: feat(pdf): real text with embedded font subsets, PDF layers (OCG), multi-sheet PDF, hyperlinks; then PDF/raster underlays (gaps.md FF10)

## Summary

- text as stroked geometry, not real fonts, so it isn't selectable or searchable;
- no PDF layers (optional content groups);
- one sheet per file.

There is also no PDF underlay (PDFATTACH) and no raster image attach.

- **Layers:** each drawing layer becomes an optional content group (on/off as in the drawing, frozen layers omitted); the option is in PLOT/EXPORTPDF and PDFLAYERS-like settings.
- **Multi-sheet:** EXPORTPDF/PUBLISH of several layouts into one PDF with page labels (layout names); stays compatible with our open #186 (Batch Publish).
- **Hyperlinks:** entity hyperlinks (PE_URL) become link annotations.
- The PDF writer stays pure Rust and wasm-safe; caps on font data and page count.

## Scope, part 2 (follow-up)

title: fix(gpu): handle uncaptured wgpu errors gracefully and avoid unstable GL backend on Windows
author: mahmagha
body:
### Description

When opening CADCraft on Windows and loading a DWG drawing, the application can crash with an unhandled `wgpu` panic during surface reconfiguration:

```
ERROR [main] wgpu::backend::wgpu_core: Handling wgpu errors as fatal by default

thread 'main' panicked at wgpu-30.0.1\src\backend\wgpu_core.rs:3981:18:
wgpu error: Validation Error

Caused by:
  In Surface::configure
    Failed to wait for GPU to come idle before reconfiguring the Surface
```

### Environment
- **OS**: Windows 11 / Windows 10 x86_64
- **CADCraft version**: 0.5.0
- **GPU**: Intel(R) UHD Graphics 620 (Driver 31.0.101.2135)

### Root Cause
1. **Uncaptured wgpu errors are treated as fatal:**
   `cadcraft_ui_egui::gpu::install` does not register an uncaptured error handler via `rs.device.on_uncaptured_error(...)`. When `wgpu` encounters an error during surface configuration or rendering (such as a `GpuWaitTimeout` when waiting for the GPU to idle), it defaults to treating the error as fatal and panics the entire process. This violates CADCraft's "Never crash" guarantee and causes users to lose open drawings.

2. **OpenGL backend instability on Windows:**
   PR #31 restricted the default Windows wgpu instance to DirectX 12 to avoid AMD's `atio6axx.dll` crash, but still allowed `WGPU_BACKEND` environment overrides to select `GL` (`create.instance_descriptor.backends = backend_override.unwrap_or(Backends::DX12)`). On Windows with Intel graphics, the OpenGL backend (`wgpu-hal::gles`) frequently times out during `Surface::configure` on drawing loads or window resizes, triggering the fatal crash.

### Proposed Solution
1. Register `device.on_uncaptured_error(...)` in `cadcraft_ui_egui::gpu::install` to log `wgpu` errors instead of panicking the application.
2. In `apps/cadcraft/src/graphics.rs`, disallow / filter out the unstable `GL` backend on Windows even if present in `WGPU_BACKEND`, logging a warning and falling back to DirectX 12.

title: DWG round-trip compatibility test with AutoCAD 2027 — results
author: neronek22
body:
Hi Brandon,

We performed a practical DWG round-trip compatibility test between AutoCAD 2027 and CADCraft on Windows 11.

We would like to share the results for your information.

### Test procedure

1. Opened a test DXF drawing in AutoCAD 2027.
2. Saved it as DWG.
3. Ran the AutoCAD `AUDIT` command — **0 errors**.
4. Opened the DWG file in CADCraft.
5. Saved the drawing as a new DWG file using CADCraft.
6. Reopened the CADCraft-generated DWG in AutoCAD 2027.
7. Ran `AUDIT` again, without applying repairs.

### Results

| Test | Original AutoCAD DWG | CADCraft-generated DWG |
|---|---|---|
| DWG format signature | AC1032 (DWG 2018) | AC1018 (DWG 2004) |
| AutoCAD AUDIT | 0 errors | 6 errors |
| File opens in AutoCAD | Yes | Yes |
| Visual appearance | Correct | Appears correct |

AutoCAD reported the following diagnostic entry during the audit:

`AcDbTableStyle(1109) - not fixed`

The audit reported 6 errors, 0 repaired, and 0 erased objects.

AutoCAD also displayed its standard warning about a DWG file saved by a non-Autodesk application.

### Test files

- `CADCraft_AutoCAD_test_01.dwg` — original AutoCAD-generated file
- `CADCraft_tu_AutoCAD_test_02.dwg` — file saved by CADCraft

We can provide both test files if they would be useful.

We are sharing these observations simply as real-world interoperability test results that may help with the project's development.

Best regards,  
**Echo Rozumu & Gadajło**

title: [Windows] 0.5.0 exits at startup: DXC runtime (dxcompiler.dll + dxil.dll) not shipped -> "Parent device is lost"
author: engmgs
body:
**cadcraft 0.5.0 (portable x64 zip and MSI, 2026-10-07 release) exits ~0.1 s after the window appears (exit code 1)** on Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26100, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (driver 32.0.16.1088), DirectX 12 default backend.

Same root cause as storytold/craft-launcher#126 (opened the same day) and storytold/lightcraft#471 (fixed there by #484). Of the twelve Craft apps installed on this machine the same log appears in wordcraft 0.5.0, gridcraft 0.5.0, deckcraft 0.5.0, soundcraft 0.5.0, vectorcraft 0.9.0; photocraft, filmcraft, lightcraft, pdfcraft, effectcraft and designcraft tolerate it.

**Log** (`%APPDATA%\CADCraft\logs\cadcraft.log`, identical every start):
```
ERROR [main] wgpu_core::indirect_validation: indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("DXC compile error: warning: DXIL signing library (dxil.dll,libdxil.so) not found.  Resulting DXIL will not be signed for use in release environments.\r\n\n"))
WARN  [main] gpu_allocator::allocator::free_list_allocator: leak detected: { ... (wgpu internal) zero init buffer ... }
ERROR [main] eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
```

2. A **matched** `dxcompiler.dll` + `dxil.dll` pair next to `<app>.exe` -> starts on DX12 from a plain double-click, no env var. Pair used: the one shipped with Microsoft Edge 154.0.4258.62.
3. `dxil.dll` alone (Chrome 154's copy) is **not** enough: `DXC compile error: error: validation errors / DXIL container mismatch for 'PSVRuntimeInfoSize' between 'PSV0' part:('48') an…

title: SpaceMouse (gaps.md H1): raw HID works natively on Windows without 3DxWare, measurements from a SpaceNavigator
author: alexanderalber
body:
`docs/gaps.md` lists H1 "3Dconnexion SpaceMouse (needs the device and 3D views)" as needing a human with the device. I have a classic SpaceNavigator (VID 046d, PID c626) on Windows 11 and would like to help with this.

**Proposal:** start with 2D navigation now (pan from the lateral axes, zoom from push/pull plus twist, tilt unused), leave orbit for when 3D views exist (F24). Read the device as raw HID, without the proprietary 3Dconnexion SDK, which keeps it clean-room and pure Rust.

**Measured** with a small probe (hidapi 2.6.7, `windows-native` feature, no 3DxWare installed):

- One HID interface, usage page 0x01 / usage 0x08. `open()` succeeds, 0 read errors.
- Layout: report 1 = tx/ty/tz, report 2 = rx/ry/rz, each 3 × int16 little-endian; report 3 = button byte (padded to 6 bytes on Windows). Newer firmware is known to pack all six axes into a 12-byte report 1; the parser should accept both. I can only test the old layout.
- The device streams continuously, also at rest: 125 reports/s. So the canvas should sample the latest state once per frame, not redraw per report.
- Full deflection reaches about ±400 to ±470 counts, not the ±350 often quoted.
- Resting offset is non-zero and not stable: at startup up to −20 counts on rx/ry, after use it moved by up to ~10 counts on other axes. A bias measured at rest plus a small deadzone (~0.03 to 0.06 of full scale) handles both; deadzone alone would have to be so wide that fine movements are lost.

**Not tested:** whether reading works while 3DxWare is installed. In the browser (WebHID) the driver claims the device and `open()` fails; for a native app on Windows I don't know. If it fails, CADCraft should say so in the UI ("3D mouse busy, possibly 3DxWare") instead of silently doing nothing. Someone with 3DxWare installed would need to check this, and macOS/Linux too.

**Web build:** the same approach works over WebHID (Chromium only). I use it in a JS tool already, including a pan/zoom mapping that scales pan speed with …

author: switch87
body:
## Survey result (2026-10-11, Linux)

I tested what CADCraft can and cannot open, headlessly, with one small real file per format

| File | Result |

| `control.dxf` | opens (`{"counts": {"Line": 1}}`) |

| `sample.FCStd` (FreeCAD) | `unsupported file type `fcstd`` |

`crates/io/src/lib.rs::read` accepts DXF (ASCII/binary) and DWG only; every other extension

CADCraft can **write** SVG (`crates/io/src/svg.rs`, offered in the Save dialog and in

Linux — cannot be opened back. For a 2D drafting app on Linux this is the single most visible
hole: DXF/DWG round-trip is strong, and the one open vector standard that every neighbouring
tool (Inkscape, QCAD's SVG pipeline, KiCad, laser software) exchanges is missing. PDF import is
already tracked (gaps.md FF10, `docs/file-format-parity.md`); SVG import is not tracked anywhere,
which is why this issue exists.

title: 0.5.0: MTEXT in the stroke font renders with no inter-word spaces (TEXT and \~ keep theirs; DXF is correct)
author: charles-hood
body:
**Environment:** cadcraft-cli 0.5.0, macOS universal zip, Apple silicon. Source read at `main` (b6383b5); I could not build `main`, so the observations are from the 0.5.0 binary.

## What happens

MTEXT set in the built-in stroke font (the `Standard` style with no TrueType face) renders with no space between words. The DXF is correct; only the rendering loses the spaces.

```
$ cadcraft-cli run \
    --cmd 'mtext {"at":[0,20],"text":"STROKE NOWIDTH two words","height":2}' \
    --cmd 'text  {"at":[0,10],"text":"TEXT two words here","height":2}' \
    --cmd 'zoom {"extents":true}' --save m.dxf --export m.png
```

`m.png` shows `STROKENOWIDTHtwowords` on the first line and `TEXT two words here`, spaced correctly, on the second. ezdxf 1.4.4 reads `m.dxf` and reports the MTEXT text as `'STROKE NOWIDTH two words'`, style `Standard`, so the stored entity is fine.

Variants, all MTEXT, height 2, same style:

| MTEXT text | Rendered |
|---|---|
| `A B single` | `ABsingle` |
| `A  B  double` | `ABdouble` |
| `A\~B nbsp` | `A Bnbsp` (the non-breaking space keeps its width) |
| `wrap at spaces when width is set here`, width 30 | wraps to `wrapatspaceswhen` / `widthissethere` |
| `A B with wf`, width_factor 1.5 | `ABwithwf` |
| TEXT `TEXT A B keeps spaces` | correct |

So the layout still finds the word boundaries (the width-constrained case wraps at the right words) and `\~` is drawn with a width, but the ordinary inter-word space is laid out at zero width. With a TrueType text style (`style` set to Arial) MTEXT keeps its spaces, so this is specific to the stroke font path.

## Where I looked

In `crates/fonts/src/mtext.rs` (`layout_mtext_with`, v0.5.0 line 477), the space between words is sized as

```rust

```

title: Panic: 657 MB egui_index_buffer exceeds wgpu max buffer size after ViewCube click on Autodesk sample DWG (1,380 entities)
author: n1byn1kt
body:
## Summary
CADCraft 0.5.0 panics after a ViewCube click on a small public Autodesk sample DWG. The drawing has only 1,380 entities, but CADCraft tries to allocate a **657 MB** egui index buffer. wgpu's maximum buffer size is 256 MB.

## Reproduce
1. Download Autodesk's official sample [`architectural_-_annotation_scaling_and_multileaders.dwg`](https://download.autodesk.com/us/samplefiles/acad/architectural_-_annotation_scaling_and_multileaders.dwg) (189 KB, AC1021 / AutoCAD 2007). It's listed on https://autodesk.com/autocad-samples.
2. Open it with `cadcraft <file>`. It displays fine.
3. Pan and zoom a little, then click one of the ViewCube's 2D arrows.
4. CADCraft panics:

```
ERROR [main] wgpu::backend::wgpu_core: Handling wgpu errors as fatal by default
thread 'main' (2) panicked at .../wgpu-30.0.1/src/backend/wgpu_core.rs:1619:18:
wgpu error: Validation Error
Caused by:
  In Device::create_buffer, label = 'egui_index_buffer'
    Buffer size 656893524 is greater than the maximum buffer size (268435456)
```

## What the file contains
From `cadcraft-cli info`:

```
Line 1178, Arc 56, Polyline 32, Dimension 28, Proxy 36, Block Reference 16, Hatch 14, MText 5, Circle 2
entityCount 1380, extents ~[2.5, 13.7] – [1337.2, 580.4] (imperial)
```

With so few entities, a 657 MB index buffer suggests one entity's tessellation exploded after the view change. My guess is a pattern hatch whose density goes unbounded when the view changes, for example a pattern scale interpreted at the wrong units, or a ViewCube rotation turning the hatch edge-on. That's a guess, not verified.

- Clamp the tessellation: cap pattern-line count per hatch (AutoCAD falls back to drawing a solid or the outline past its `HPMAXLINES` limit, 1,000,000 by default), and split or cap the egui mesh before it reaches `max_buffer_size`.

title: Canvas freezes on zoom: filled TrueType text costs ~195 triangles per character, rebuilt every zoom band (16M triangles, 2.7 s per step)
author: codyvogt
body:
## Summary

On a real survey plan (DWG, 6,434 entities), every 2x zoom step freezes the canvas for about 2.7 s. Entity count isn't the problem: **filled TrueType text is.** Every glyph is triangulated by the slab decomposition in `fill::triangulate_evenodd` at about 195 triangles per character, whatever its size on screen, and nothing is cached, so the canvas redoes it for every character at every zoom band.

This is the text counterpart of #544 (pattern hatches), which #638 fixes for hatches only.

## Measurements

`main` at 54ea5e7, Windows 11, dev profile (`opt-level` as configured in the workspace, which is optimised). The drawing has 8 TABLE entities (layer legends, 7 columns, 9–93 rows), about 76k characters in Arial Narrow, plus 97 MTEXT.

From the running app (`ui.inspect` → `perf`) after a wheel zoom crosses a band:

| | ms |
|---|---|
| `buildMs` (display list) | 1,910 |
| `meshMs` (vertex data) | 780 |

Headless, `cadcraft_render::build` on model space as `ensure_list` calls it (1000 px view of the extents):

| Build | ms | Triangles |
|---|---|---|
| As drawn (TEXTFILL 1) | 1,308 | 16.1 M |
| TEXTFILL 0 (glyph outlines) | 117 | ~0 (5.4 M line verts) |
| `Options { text: false }` | 7 | 46 k |

Per entity type (build_entities on each top-level entity): the 8 tables take 1,249 ms and 44 M triangle vertices; 97 MTEXT 89 ms and 3.6 M; the other 6,300 entities (3,841 inserts included) about 15 ms together. Per table, triangles per character are a steady 189–213.

## Cause

- `ttf.rs` flattens each quadratic segment into 6 steps and each cubic into 8, in font units, regardless of on-screen size.
- `Builder::shaped` fills each glyph with `fill::triangulate_evenodd`, which cuts a horizontal slab at every distinct vertex y. A glyph with ~100 outline points gives ~100 slabs × 2–4 crossings → hundreds of triangles; ear clipping or monotone triangulation would give about n.
- The result depends on nothing that changes with zoom, yet it is rebuilt from scratch on ever…
